3.6.d:
सम्पूर्णे सप्तमे वर्षे मित्रावरुणसंज्ञकौ ।
मुनी तस्याश्रमं प्राप्तौ द्रष्टुं मां चाज्ञया विभोः ॥
3.6.m: When the seventh year was completed, two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa / arrived at his hermitage to see me, by the command of the Lord.

3.6.s:
satkṛtau muninā tena sūpaviṣṭo mahāmunī |
ūcatuśca mahātmānau māṃ nirīkṣya muhurmuhuḥ ||
3.6.d:
सत्कृतौ मुनिना तेन सूपविष्टो महामुनी ।
ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ मां निरीक्ष्य मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
3.6.m: Hospitably received by that sage and well seated, the two great sages, / noble-minded, spoke, looking at me again and again.

3.6.s:
mitrāvaruṇāvūcatuḥ |
tāta nandī tavālpāyuḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ |
na dṛṣṭameva cāpaśyaṃ hyāyurvarṣādataḥ param ||
3.6.d:
मित्रावरुणावूचतुः ।
तात नन्दी तवाल्पायुः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ।
न दृष्टमेव चापश्यं ह्यायुर्वर्षादतः परम् ॥
3.6.m: Mitra and Varuṇa said: / "Dear Nandin, your lifespan is short, though you have mastered the meaning of all treatises; / we did not see and do not see life beyond a year from now."

3.6.s:
viprayorityuktavatoḥ śilādaḥ putravatsalaḥ |
tamāliṅgya ca duḥkhārto rurodātīva visvaram ||
3.6.d:
विप्रयोरित्युक्तवतोः शिलादः पुत्रवत्सलः ।
तमालिङ्ग्य च दुःखार्तो रुरोदातीव विस्वरम् ॥
3.6.m: When the two brahmins had spoken thus, Śilāda, affectionate toward his son, / embraced him and, afflicted with grief, wept in a discordant voice.

3.6.s:
mṛtavatpatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ ca pitāmaham |
pratyavocatprasannātmā smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam ||
3.6.d:
मृतवत्पतितं दृष्ट्वा पितरं च पितामहम् ।
प्रत्यवोचत्प्रसन्नात्मा स्मृत्वा शिवपदाम्बुजम् ॥
3.6.m: Seeing his father and forefathers fallen as if dead, / [Nandin], serene in soul, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, answered:

3.6.s:
kena tvaṃ tāta duḥkhena vepamānaśca rodiṣi |
duḥkhaṃ te kuta utpannaṃ jñātumicchāmi tattvataḥ ||
3.6.d:
केन त्वं तात दुःखेन वेपमानश्च रोदिषि ।
दुःखं ते कुत उत्पन्नं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥
3.6.m: "Father, from what sorrow do you weep, trembling? / Whence has your sorrow arisen? I wish to know in truth."

3.6.s:
pitovāca |
tavālpamṛtyuduḥkhena duḥkhito'tīva putraka |
ko me duḥkhaṃ haratu vai śaraṇaṃ taṃ prayāmi hi ||
3.6.d:
पितोवाच ।
तवाल्पमृत्युदुःखेन दुःखितोऽतीव पुत्रक ।
को मे दुःखं हरतु वै शरणं तं प्रयामि हि ॥
3.6.m: The father said: / "I am exceedingly sorrowful from the grief of your short death, dear child; / who indeed can take away my sorrow? To that refuge I shall go."

3.6.s:
putra uvāca |
devo vā dānavo vāpi yamaḥ kālo'thavāpi hi |
ṛdhyeyuryadyapi hyete māmanye'pi janāstathā ||
3.6.d:
पुत्र उवाच ।
देवो वा दानवो वापि यमः कालोऽथवापि हि ।
ऋध्येयुर्यद्यपि ह्येते मामन्येऽपि जनास्तथा ॥
3.6.m: The son said: / "Whether god or Dānava, Yama or Time itself, / even if these and other beings were to prosper against me,

3.6.s:
athāpi cālpamṛtyurme na bhaviṣyati mā tudaḥ |
satyaṃ bravīmi janaka śapathaṃ te karomyaham ||
3.6.d:
अथापि चाल्पमृत्युर्मे न भविष्यति मा तुदः ।
सत्यं ब्रवीमि जनक शपथं ते करोम्यहम् ॥
3.6.m: even so, an untimely death shall not be mine; do not grieve! / I speak truth, father; I make an oath to you."

3.6.s:
pitovāca |
kiṃ tapaḥ kiṃ parijñānaṃ ko yogaśca prabhuśca te |
yena tvaṃ dāruṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ vañcayiṣyasi putra me ||
3.6.d:
पितोवाच ।
किं तपः किं परिज्ञानं को योगश्च प्रभुश्च ते ।
येन त्वं दारुणं दुःखं वञ्चयिष्यसि पुत्र मे ॥
3.6.m: The father said: / "What austerity, what profound knowledge, what yoga, and what master is yours, / by which you will avert this terrible sorrow, O my son?"

3.6.s:
putra uvāca |
na tāta tapasā mṛtyuṃ vañcayiṣye na vidyayā |
mahādevasya bhajanānmṛtyuṃ jeṣyāmi nānyathā ||
3.6.d:
पुत्र उवाच ।
न तात तपसा मृत्युं वञ्चयिष्ये न विद्यया ।
महादेवस्य भजनान्मृत्युं जेष्यामि नान्यथा ॥

3.6.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvāhaṃ pituḥ pādau praṇamya śirasā mune |
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca tamagacchaṃ vanamuttamam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.6.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वाहं पितुः पादौ प्रणम्य शिरसा मुने ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य च तमगच्छं वनमुत्तमम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.6.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Having said this, O sage, bowing my head to my father's feet
and circumambulating him, I went to an excellent forest.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Incarnation of Nandikeśa', in the third [section], the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, of the auspicious Śivapurāṇa.

3.7.s:
nandikeśvara uvāca |
tatra gatvā mune'haṃ vai sthitvaikāntasthale sudhīḥ |
atapaṃ tapa ugraṃ sanmunīnāmapi duṣkaram ||
3.7.d:
नन्दिकेश्वर उवाच ।
तत्र गत्वा मुनेऽहं वै स्थित्वैकान्तस्थले सुधीः ।
अतपं तप उग्रं सन्मुनीनामपि दुष्करम् ॥
3.7.m:
Nandikeśvara said:
Having gone there, O sage, staying in a solitary place, resolute in mind,
I performed fierce austerity, difficult even for sages to accomplish.

3.7.s:
hṛtpuṇḍarīkasuṣire dhyātvā devaṃ triyambakam |
tryakṣaṃ daśabhujaṃ śāntaṃ pañcavaktraṃ sadāśivam ||
3.7.d:
हृत्पुण्डरीकसुषिरे ध्यात्वा देवं त्रियम्बकम् ।
त्र्यक्षं दशभुजं शान्तं पञ्चवक्त्रं सदाशिवम् ॥
3.7.m:
Meditating in the cavity of the heart-lotus upon the god Tryambaka,
three-eyed, ten-armed, peaceful, five-faced, Sadāśiva,

3.7.s:
rudrajāpyamakārṣaṃ vai paramadhyānamāsthitaḥ |
saritaścottare puṇye hyekacittaḥ samāhitaḥ ||
3.7.d:
रुद्रजाप्यमकार्षं वै परमध्यानमास्थितः ।
सरितश्चोत्तरे पुण्ये ह्येकचित्तः समाहितः ॥
3.7.m:
I performed the recitation of Rudra, established in supreme meditation,
on the holy northern [bank] of the river, single-minded and concentrated.

3.7.s:
tasmiñjāpye'tha samprītaḥ sthitaṃ māṃ parameśvaraḥ |
tuṣṭo'bravīnmahādevaḥ somaḥ somārddhabhūṣaṇaḥ ||
3.7.d:
तस्मिञ्जाप्येऽथ सम्प्रीतः स्थितं मां परमेश्वरः ।
तुष्टोऽब्रवीन्महादेवः सोमः सोमार्द्धभूषणः ॥
3.7.m:
Pleased with that recitation, to me who stood there, Parameśvara,
Mahādeva, accompanied by Umā and adorned with the crescent moon, spoke with delight.

3.7.s:
śiva uvāca |
śailāde varado'haṃ te tapasānena toṣitaḥ |
sādhu taptaṃ tvayā dhīman brūhi yatte manogatam ||
3.7.d:
शिव उवाच ।
शैलादे वरदोऽहं ते तपसानेन तोषितः ।
साधु तप्तं त्वया धीमन् ब्रूहि यत्ते मनोगतम् ॥
3.7.m:
Śiva said:
O Śailāda, I am the giver of boons to you, pleased by this austerity.
Well have you performed austerity, O wise one! Speak what is in your heart.

3.7.s:
sa evamukto devena śirasā pādayornataḥ |
astavaṃ parameśānaṃ jarāśokavināśanam ||
3.7.d:
स एवमुक्तो देवेन शिरसा पादयोर्नतः ।
अस्तवं परमेशानं जराशोकविनाशनम् ॥
3.7.m:
Thus addressed by the god, bowing with my head at his feet,
I praised Parameśāna, the destroyer of old age and sorrow.

3.7.s:
atha māṃ nandinaṃ śambhurbhaktyā parāmayā yutam |
aśrupūrṇekṣaṇaṃ samyak pādayoḥ śirasā natam ||
3.7.d:
अथ मां नन्दिनं शम्भुर्भक्त्या परामया युतम् ।
अश्रुपूर्णेक्षणं सम्यक् पादयोः शिरसा नतम् ॥
3.7.m:
Then Śambhu [looked upon] me, Nandin, endowed with supreme devotion,
my eyes filled with tears, duly bowing my head at his feet.

3.7.s:
utthāpya parameśānaḥ pasparśa paramārtihā |
karābhyāṃ sammukhābhyāṃ tu saṅgṛhya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ||
3.7.d:
उत्थाप्य परमेशानः पस्पर्श परमार्तिहा ।
कराभ्यां सम्मुखाभ्यां तु सङ्गृह्य वृषभध्वजः ॥
3.7.m:
Raising [me] up, Parameśāna, the destroyer of supreme distress, touched [me];
and taking hold [of me] with both hands right before him, Vṛṣabhadhvaja,

3.7.s:
nirīkṣya gaṇapāṃścaiva devīṃ himavataḥ sutām |
uvāca māṃ kṛpādṛṣṭyā samīkṣya jagatāṃ patiḥ ||
3.7.d:
निरीक्ष्य गणपांश्चैव देवीं हिमवतः सुताम् ।
उवाच मां कृपादृष्ट्या समीक्ष्य जगतां पतिः ॥
3.7.m:
looking upon the lords of the attendants and the goddess, the daughter of the Himavat,
the Lord of the worlds, looking upon me with a glance of compassion, spoke:

3.7.s:
vatsa nandin mahāprājña mṛtyorbhītiḥ kutastava |
mayaiva preṣitau viprau matsamastvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
3.7.d:
वत्स नन्दिन् महाप्राज्ञ मृत्योर्भीतिः कुतस्तव ।
मयैव प्रेषितौ विप्रौ मत्समस्त्वं न संशयः ॥
3.7.m:
Dear Nandin, highly wise one, whence is your fear of death?
By me alone were the two brahmins sent; you are equal to me, there is no doubt.

3.7.s:
amaro jarayā tyakto'duḥkhī gaṇapatiḥ sadā |
avyayaścākṣayaśceṣṭaḥ sapitā sasuhṛjjanaḥ ||
3.7.d:
अमरो जरया त्यक्तोऽदुःखी गणपतिः सदा ।
अव्ययश्चाक्षयश्चेष्टः सपिता ससुहृज्जनः ॥
3.7.m:
Immortal, free from old age, without sorrow, forever a lord of attendants,
imperishable and inexhaustible, beloved, along with your father and friends,

3.7.s:
madbalaḥ pārśvago nityaṃ mameṣṭo bhavitāniśam |
na jarā janma mṛtyurvai matprasādādbhaviṣyati ||
3.7.d:
मद्बलः पार्श्वगो नित्यं ममेष्टो भवितानिशम् ।
न जरा जन्म मृत्युर्वै मत्प्रसादाद्भविष्यति ॥
3.7.m:
possessing my strength, always by my side, you shall continually be dear to me;
neither old age, birth, nor death shall befall [you] by my grace.

3.7.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
evamuktvā śiromālāṃ kuśeśayamayīṃ nijām |
samunmucya babandhāśu mama kaṇṭhe kṛpānidhiḥ ||
3.7.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा शिरोमालां कुशेशयमयीं निजाम् ।
समुन्मुच्य बबन्धाशु मम कण्ठे कृपानिधिः ॥
3.7.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Having spoken thus, the ocean of compassion took off his own crest-garland
made of lotus flowers and quickly fastened it around my neck.

3.7.s:
tayāhaṃ mālayā vipra śubhayā kaṇṭhasaktayā |
tryakṣo daśabhujaścāsaṃ dvitīya iva śaṅkaraḥ ||
3.7.d:
तयाहं मालया विप्र शुभया कण्ठसक्तया ।
त्र्यक्षो दशभुजश्चासं द्वितीय इव शङ्करः ॥
3.7.m:
By that auspicious garland fastened to my neck, O brahmin,
I became three-eyed and ten-armed, like a second Śaṅkara.

3.7.s:
tata eva samādāya hastena parameśvaraḥ |
uvāca brūhi kiṃ te'dya dadāmi varamuttamam ||
3.7.d:
तत एव समादाय हस्तेन परमेश्वरः ।
उवाच ब्रूहि किं तेऽद्य ददामि वरमुत्तमम् ॥
3.7.m:
Taking [me] with his hand from that very spot, Parameśvara
said: 'Speak, what excellent boon shall I give you today?'

3.7.s:
tato jaṭāśritaṃ vāri gṛhītvā hāranirmalam |
uktvā nadī bhavetīha visasarja vṛṣadhvajaḥ ||
3.7.d:
ततो जटाश्रितं वारि गृहीत्वा हारनिर्मलम् ।
उक्त्वा नदी भवेतीह विससर्ज वृषध्वजः ॥
3.7.m:
Then, taking the water resting in his matted hair, pure as a necklace of pearls,
and saying 'Become a river here', Vṛṣadhvaja released [it].

3.7.s:
tataḥ pañcamitā nadyaḥ prāvartanta śubhāvahāḥ |
sutoyāśca mahāvegā divyarūpā ca sundarīḥ ||
3.7.d:
ततः पञ्चमिता नद्यः प्रावर्तन्त शुभावहाः ।
सुतोयाश्च महावेगा दिव्यरूपा च सुन्दरीः ॥
3.7.m:
From that, five auspicious rivers began to flow,
having excellent waters, great speed, celestial form, and beautiful;

3.7.s:
jaṭodakā trisrotāśca vṛṣadhvaniritīva hi |
svarṇodakā jambunadī pañca nadyaḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
3.7.d:
जटोदका त्रिस्रोताश्च वृषध्वनिरितीव हि ।
स्वर्णोदका जम्बुनदी पञ्च नद्यः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
3.7.m:
Jaṭodakā, Trisrotā, and Vṛṣadhvani indeed,
Svarṇodakā, and Jambunadī: these are renowned as the five rivers.

3.7.s:
etatpañcanadaṃ nāma śivapṛṣṭhatamaṃ śubham |
japeśvarasamīpe tu pavitraṃ paramaṃ mune ||
3.7.d:
एतत्पञ्चनदं नाम शिवपृष्ठतमं शुभम् ।
जपेश्वरसमीपे तु पवित्रं परमं मुने ॥
3.7.m:
This is named Pañcanada, most beloved of Śiva, auspicious,
near Japeśvara, exceedingly holy, O sage.

3.7.s:
yaḥ pañcanadamāsādya snātvā japtveśvareśvaram |
pūjayecchivasāyujyaṃ prayātyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
3.7.d:
यः पञ्चनदमासाद्य स्नात्वा जप्त्वेश्वरेश्वरम् ।
पूजयेच्छिवसायुज्यं प्रयात्येव न संशयः ॥
3.7.m:
Whoever, having reached Pañcanada, bathes, recites, and worships
the Lord of lords, indeed attains communion with Śiva; there is no doubt.

3.7.s:
atha śambhuruvācomāmabhiṣiñcāmi nandinam |
gaṇendraṃ vyāhariṣyāmi kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase'vyaye ||
3.7.d:
अथ शम्भुरुवाचोमामभिषिञ्चामि नन्दिनम् ।
गणेन्द्रं व्याहरिष्यामि किं वा त्वं मन्यसेऽव्यये ॥
3.7.m:
Then Śambhu said to Umā: 'I shall consecrate Nandin;
I shall declare him sovereign of the attendants. What do you think, O imperishable one?'

3.7.s:
umovāca |
dātumarhasi deveśa nandine parameśvara |
mahāpriyatamo nātha śailādistanayo mama ||
3.7.d:
उमोवाच ।
दातुमर्हसि देवेश नन्दिने परमेश्वर ।
महाप्रियतमो नाथ शैलादिस्तनयो मम ॥

3.7.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
tataḥ sa śaṅkaraḥ svīyānsasmāra gaṇapānvarān |
svatantraḥ parameśānaḥ sarvado bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
3.7.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
ततः स शङ्करः स्वीयान्सस्मार गणपान्वरान् ।
स्वतन्त्रः परमेशानः सर्वदो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
3.7.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Then Śaṅkara remembered his own excellent lords of the attendants—
independent, Parameśāna, all-bestowing, affectionate toward devotees.

3.7.s:
smaraṇādeva rudrasya samprāptāśca gaṇeśvarāḥ |
asaṅkhyātā mahāmodāḥ śaṅkarākṛtayo'khilāḥ ||
3.7.d:
स्मरणादेव रुद्रस्य सम्प्राप्ताश्च गणेश्वराः ।
असङ्ख्याता महामोदाः शङ्कराकृतयोऽखिलाः ॥
3.7.m:
Merely upon the remembrance by Rudra, the lords of the attendants arrived,
innumerable, full of great joy, all having the form of Śaṅkara.

3.7.s:
te gaṇeśāḥ śivaṃ devīṃ praṇamyāhuḥ śubhaṃ vacaḥ |
te praṇamya karau baddhvā nataskandhā mahābalāḥ ||
3.7.d:
ते गणेशाः शिवं देवीं प्रणम्याहुः शुभं वचः ।
ते प्रणम्य करौ बद्ध्वा नतस्कन्धा महाबलाः ॥
3.7.m:
Those lords of the attendants, bowing to Śiva and the goddess, spoke an auspicious word;
having bowed, joining their hands, with shoulders bent, very mighty.

3.7.s:
gaṇeśā ūcuḥ |
kimarthaṃ ca smṛtā deva hyājñāpaya mahāprabho |
kiṅkarānnaḥ samāyātāṃstripurārdana kāmada ||
3.7.d:
गणेशा ऊचुः ।
किमर्थं च स्मृता देव ह्याज्ञापय महाप्रभो ।
किङ्करान्नः समायातांस्त्रिपुरार्दन कामद ॥
3.7.m:
The lords of the attendants said:
For what purpose have we been remembered, O God? Order us, O Great Lord,
us, your servants who have arrived, O Destroyer of Tripura, O granter of desires!

3.7.s:
kiṃ sāgarān śoṣayāmo yamaṃ vā saha kiṅkaraiḥ |
hanmo mṛtyuṃ mahāmṛtyuṃ viśeṣaṃ vṛddhapadmajam ||
3.7.d:
किं सागरान् शोषयामो यमं वा सह किङ्करैः ।
हन्मो मृत्युं महामृत्युं विशेषं वृद्धपद्मजम् ॥
3.7.m:
Shall we dry up the oceans, or Yama together with his servants?
Shall we slay death, great death, especially the aged lotus-born [Brahmā]?

3.7.s:
baddhvendraṃ saha devaiśca viṣṇuṃ vā pārṣadaiḥ saha |
ānayāmaḥ susaṅkruddhāndaityānvā dānavaiḥ saha ||
3.7.d:
बद्ध्वेन्द्रं सह देवैश्च विष्णुं वा पार्षदैः सह ।
आनयामः सुसङ्क्रुद्धान्दैत्यान्वा दानवैः सह ॥
3.7.m:
Binding Indra along with the gods, or Viṣṇu along with his attendants,
shall we bring [them], or the fiercely enraged Daityas along with the Dānavas?

3.7.s:
kasyādya vyasanaṃ ghoraṃ kariṣyāmastavājñayā |
kasya vādyotsavo deva sarvakāmasamṛddhaye ||
3.7.d:
कस्याद्य व्यसनं घोरं करिष्यामस्तवाज्ञया ।
कस्य वाद्योत्सवो देव सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥
3.7.m:
Whose terrible ruin shall we bring about today at your command?
Or for whose sake today is there a festival, O God, for the fulfillment of all desires?

3.7.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ gaṇānāṃ vīravādinām |
uvāca tānsa praśaṃsya gaṇeśānparameśvaraḥ ||
3.7.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तेषां गणानां वीरवादिनाम् ।
उवाच तान्स प्रशंस्य गणेशान्परमेश्वरः ॥
3.7.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Having heard this speech of those attendants, speaking like heroes,
Parameśvara, having praised those lords of the attendants, said to them:

3.7.s:
śiva uvāca |
nandīśvaro'yaṃ putro me sarveṣāmīśvareśvaraḥ |
priyo gaṇāgraṇīḥ sarvaiḥ kriyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama ||
3.7.d:
शिव उवाच ।
नन्दीश्वरोऽयं पुत्रो मे सर्वेषामीश्वरेश्वरः ।
प्रियो गणाग्रणीः सर्वैः क्रियतां वचनं मम ॥
3.7.m:
Śiva said:
This Nandīśvara is my son, the Lord of lords over all,
dear to me, the leader of the attendants; let my word be carried out by all.

3.7.s:
sarve prītyābhiṣiñcadhvaṃ madgaṇānāṃ gatiṃ patim |
adyaprabhṛti yuṣmākamayaṃ nandīśvaraḥ prabhuḥ ||
3.7.d:
सर्वे प्रीत्याभिषिञ्चध्वं मद्गणानां गतिं पतिम् ।
अद्यप्रभृति युष्माकमयं नन्दीश्वरः प्रभुः ॥
3.7.m:
All of you consecrate with affection the refuge and master of my attendants;
from this day forward, this Nandīśvara is your lord.

3.7.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
evamuktāḥ śaṅkareṇa gaṇapāḥ sarva eva te |
evamastviti samprocya sambhārānāharam̐stataḥ ||
3.7.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एवमुक्ताः शङ्करेण गणपाः सर्व एव ते ।
एवमस्त्विति सम्प्रोच्य सम्भारानाहरम्̐स्ततः ॥
3.7.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, all those lords of the attendants,
having said 'So be it', then brought the materials.

3.7.s:
tato devāśca sendrāśca nārāyaṇamukhāstathā |
munayaḥ sarvato lokā ājagmurmuditānanāḥ ||
3.7.d:
ततो देवाश्च सेन्द्राश्च नारायणमुखास्तथा ।
मुनयः सर्वतो लोका आजग्मुर्मुदिताननाः ॥
3.7.m:
Then the gods led by Indra, and likewise those headed by Nārāyaṇa,
sages, and people from all quarters arrived with joyful faces.

3.7.s:
pitāmaho'pi bhagavanniyogācchaṅkarasya vai |
cakāra nandinaḥ sarvamabhiṣekaṃ samāhitaḥ ||
3.7.d:
पितामहोऽपि भगवन्नियोगाच्छङ्करस्य वै ।
चकार नन्दिनः सर्वमभिषेकं समाहितः ॥
3.7.m:
Even the revered Grandfather [Brahmā], by the command of Śaṅkara,
concentrated in mind, performed the entire consecration of Nandin.

3.7.s:
tato viṣṇustataḥ śakro lokapālāstathaiva ca |
ṛṣayastuṣṭuvuścaiva pitāmahapurogamāḥ ||
3.7.d:
ततो विष्णुस्ततः शक्रो लोकपालास्तथैव च ।
ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैव पितामहपुरोगमाः ॥
3.7.m:
Then Viṣṇu, then Śakra, and likewise the guardians of the world,
and the ṛṣis, with the Grandfather at their head, sang praises.

3.7.s:
stutimatsu tatasteṣu viṣṇuḥ sarvajagatpatiḥ |
śirasyañjalimādhāya tuṣṭāva ca samāhitaḥ ||
3.7.d:
स्तुतिमत्सु ततस्तेषु विष्णुः सर्वजगत्पतिः ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय तुष्टाव च समाहितः ॥
3.7.m:
While they were offering praises, Viṣṇu, the lord of all the universe,
placing folded hands upon his head, praised [him] with a concentrated mind.

3.7.s:
prāñjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā jayaśabdaṃ cakāra ca |
tato gaṇādhipāḥ sarva tato devāstato'surāḥ ||
3.7.d:
प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतो भूत्वा जयशब्दं चकार च ।
ततो गणाधिपाः सर्व ततो देवास्ततोऽसुराः ॥
3.7.m:
With folded hands, having bowed down, he raised the shout of victory;
then all the lords of the attendants, then the gods, then the Asuras [did so].

3.7.s:
evaṃ stutaścābhiṣikto devaiḥ sabrahmakaistadā |
nandīśvarohaṃ viprendra niyogātpa rameśituḥ ||
3.7.d:
एवं स्तुतश्चाभिषिक्तो देवैः सब्रह्मकैस्तदा ।
नन्दीश्वरोहं विप्रेन्द्र नियोगात्प रमेशितुः ॥
3.7.m:
Thus praised and consecrated then by the gods along with Brahmā,
I became Nandīśvara, O best of brahmins, by command of Parameśvara.

3.7.s:
udvāhaśca kṛtastatra niyogātparameṣṭhinaḥ |
mahotsavayutaḥ prītyā viṣṇubrahmādibhirmama ||
3.7.d:
उद्वाहश्च कृतस्तत्र नियोगात्परमेष्ठिनः ।
महोत्सवयुतः प्रीत्या विष्णुब्रह्मादिभिर्मम ॥
3.7.m:
And my marriage was performed there by command of the Supreme Lord,
accompanied by a great festival, with love, by Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and others.

3.7.s:
marutāṃ ca sutā devī suyaśāstu manoharā |
patnī sā me'bhavaddivyā manonayananandinī ||
3.7.d:
मरुतां च सुता देवी सुयशास्तु मनोहरा ।
पत्नी सा मेऽभवद्दिव्या मनोनयननन्दिनी ॥
3.7.m:
The goddess Suyaśā, the charming daughter of the Maruts,
celestial and delighting the mind and eyes, became my wife.

3.7.s:
labdhaṃ śaśiprabhaṃ chatraṃ tayā tatra vibhūṣitam |
cāmaraiścāmarāsaktahastāgraiḥ strīgaṇairyutam ||
3.7.d:
लब्धं शशिप्रभं छत्रं तया तत्र विभूषितम् ।
चामरैश्चामरासक्तहस्ताग्रैः स्त्रीगणैर्युतम् ॥
3.7.m:
A parasol shining like the moon was received [by me], adorned by her there,
accompanied by groups of women with chowries held in the tips of their hands.

3.7.s:
siṃhāsanaṃ ca paramaṃ tayā cādhiṣṭhitaṃ mayā |
alaṅkṛto mahālakṣmyā mukuṭādyaiḥ subhūṣaṇaiḥ ||
3.7.d:
सिंहासनं च परमं तया चाधिष्ठितं मया ।
अलङ्कृतो महालक्ष्म्या मुकुटाद्यैः सुभूषणैः ॥
3.7.m: And an excellent throne was occupied by her and by me, / adorned with great splendor, with diadems and other fine ornaments.

3.7.s:
labdho hāraśca paramo devyāḥ kaṇṭhagatastathā |
vṛṣendraśca śito nāgassiṃhaḥ siṃhadhvajastathā ||
3.7.d:
लब्धो हारश्च परमो देव्याः कण्ठगतस्तथा ।
वृषेन्द्रश्च शितो नागस्सिंहः सिंहध्वजस्तथा ॥
3.7.m: A magnificent necklace worn on the goddess's neck was obtained, / as well as a lord of bulls, a white elephant, a lion, and a lion-bannered chariot,

3.7.s:
rathaśca hemahāraśca candrabimbasamaḥ śubhaḥ |
anyānyapi ca vastūni labdhāni hi mayā mune ||
3.7.d:
रथश्च हेमहारश्च चन्द्रबिम्बसमः शुभः ।
अन्यान्यपि च वस्तूनि लब्धानि हि मया मुने ॥
3.7.m: and a golden necklace auspicious as the disc of the moon; / and other things too were indeed obtained by me, O sage.

3.7.s:
evaṃ kṛtavivāho'haṃ tayā patnyā mahāmune |
pādau vavande śambhośca śivāyā brahmaṇo hareḥ ||
3.7.d:
एवं कृतविवाहोऽहं तया पत्न्या महामुने ।
पादौ ववन्दे शम्भोश्च शिवाया ब्रह्मणो हरेः ॥
3.7.m: Having thus been married to that wife, O great sage, / I bowed to the feet of Śambhu, of Śivā, of Brahmā, and of Hari.

3.7.s:
tathāvidhaṃ trilokeśaḥ sapatnīkaṃ ca māṃ prabhuḥ |
provāca parayā prītyā sa śivo bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
3.7.d:
तथाविधं त्रिलोकेशः सपत्नीकं च मां प्रभुः ।
प्रोवाच परया प्रीत्या स शिवो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
3.7.m: To me in that state, accompanied by my wife, the Lord, the master of the three worlds, / that Śiva affectionate toward devotees, spoke with supreme joy.

3.7.s:
īśvara uvāca |
śṛṇu satputra tātastvaṃ suyaśeyaṃ tava priyā |
dadāmi te varaṃ prītyā yatte manasi vāñchitam ||
3.7.d:
ईश्वर उवाच ।
शृणु सत्पुत्र तातस्त्वं सुयशेयं तव प्रिया ।
ददामि ते वरं प्रीत्या यत्ते मनसि वाञ्छितम् ॥
3.7.m: The Lord said: / 'Listen, good son, my dear child! This Suyaśā is your beloved; / I grant you with pleasure the boon whatever is desired in your mind.

3.7.s:
sadā'haṃ tava nandīśa santuṣṭo'smi gaṇeśvara |
devyā ca sahito vatsa śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ ||
3.7.d:
सदाऽहं तव नन्दीश सन्तुष्टोऽस्मि गणेश्वर ।
देव्या च सहितो वत्स शृणु मे परमं वचः ॥
3.7.m: I am ever pleased with you, O Nandīśa, O lord of the attendants! / Together with the goddess, my child, hear my supreme word:

3.7.s:
sadeṣṭaśca viśiṣṭaśca paramaiśvaryasaṃyutaḥ |
mahāyogī maheṣvāsaḥ sapitā sapitāmahaḥ ||
3.7.d:
सदेष्टश्च विशिष्टश्च परमैश्वर्यसंयुतः ।
महायोगी महेष्वासः सपिता सपितामहः ॥
3.7.m: Ever favored and distinguished, endowed with supreme sovereignty, / a great yogin, a great archer, along with your father and grandfather,

3.7.s:
ajeyaḥ sarvajetā ca sadā pūjyo mahābalaḥ |
ahaṃ yatra bhavāṃstatra yatra tvaṃ tatra cāpyaham ||
3.7.d:
अजेयः सर्वजेता च सदा पूज्यो महाबलः ।
अहं यत्र भवांस्तत्र यत्र त्वं तत्र चाप्यहम् ॥
3.7.m: unconquerable, conqueror of all, ever worshipful, possessed of great strength: / wherever I am, there you shall be; and wherever you are, there too shall I be.

3.7.s:
ayaṃ ca te pitā putra paramaiśvaryasaṃyutaḥ |
bhaviṣyati gaṇādhyakṣo mama bhakto mahābalaḥ ||
3.7.d:
अयं च ते पिता पुत्र परमैश्वर्यसंयुतः ।
भविष्यति गणाध्यक्षो मम भक्तो महाबलः ॥
3.7.m: And this your father, O son, endowed with supreme sovereignty, / shall be a leader of attendants, my devotee, possessed of great strength.

3.7.s:
pitāmaho'pi te vatsa tathāstu niyamā ime |
matsamīpaṃ gamiṣyanti mayā dattavarāstathā ||
3.7.d:
पितामहोऽपि ते वत्स तथास्तु नियमा इमे ।
मत्समीपं गमिष्यन्ति मया दत्तवरास्तथा ॥
3.7.m: Let it be so for your grandfather too, my child. These observances / shall bring them near to me, granted boons by me.'

3.7.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
tato devī mahābhāgā nandinaṃ varadābravīt |
varaṃ brūhīti māṃ putra sarvānkāmānyathepsitān ||
3.7.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
ततो देवी महाभागा नन्दिनं वरदाब्रवीत् ।
वरं ब्रूहीति मां पुत्र सर्वान्कामान्यथेप्सितान् ॥
3.7.m: Nandīśvara said: / 'Then the illustrious goddess, bestower of boons, said to Nandin: / "Ask for a boon, O son, all desires as you wish!"

3.7.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ devyāḥ prāvocatsāñjalistadā |
bhaktirbhavatu me devi pādayoste sadā varā ||
3.7.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं देव्याः प्रावोचत्साञ्जलिस्तदा ।
भक्तिर्भवतु मे देवि पादयोस्ते सदा वरा ॥
3.7.m: Hearing that speech of the goddess, he then spoke with folded hands: / "O goddess, may I always have excellent devotion to your feet!"

3.7.s:
śrutvā mama vaco devī hyevamastviti sābravīt |
suyaśāṃ tāṃ ca suprītyā nandipriyatamāṃ śivām ||
3.7.d:
श्रुत्वा मम वचो देवी ह्येवमस्त्विति साब्रवीत् ।
सुयशां तां च सुप्रीत्या नन्दिप्रियतमां शिवाम् ॥
3.7.m: Hearing my words, the goddess said, "So be it!", / and with great pleasure to that Suyaśā, the beloved of Nandin, the auspicious one:

3.7.s:
devyuvāca |
vatse varaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ hi trinetrā janmavarjitā |
putrapautraistu bhaktirme tathā ca bhartureva hi ||
3.7.d:
देव्युवाच ।
वत्से वरं यथेष्टं हि त्रिनेत्रा जन्मवर्जिता ।
पुत्रपौत्रैस्तु भक्तिर्मे तथा च भर्तुरेव हि ॥
3.7.m: The goddess said: / "My child, [choose] a boon as you wish: three-eyed, free from rebirth, / and with sons and grandsons, devoted to me and to your husband."

3.7.s:
nandyuvāca |
tadā brahmā ca viṣṇuśca sarve devagaṇāśca vai |
tābhyāṃ varāndaduḥ prītyā suprasannāḥ śivājñayā ||
3.7.d:
नन्द्युवाच ।
तदा ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च सर्वे देवगणाश्च वै ।
ताभ्यां वरान्ददुः प्रीत्या सुप्रसन्नाः शिवाज्ञया ॥
3.7.m: Nandin said: / 'Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and all the hosts of gods indeed, / greatly pleased, gladly gave them boons by the command of Śiva.

3.7.s:
sānvayaṃ māṃ gṛhītveśastataḥ sambandhibāndhavaiḥ |
āruhya vṛṣamīśāno gato devyā nijaṃ gṛham ||
3.7.d:
सान्वयं मां गृहीत्वेशस्ततः सम्बन्धिबान्धवैः ।
आरुह्य वृषमीशानो गतो देव्या निजं गृहम् ॥
3.7.m: Taking me along with my lineage, kin, and relatives, / the Lord mounted the bull and departed with the goddess for his own abode.

3.7.s:
viṣṇvādayaḥ surāḥ sarve praśaṃsanto hyamī tadā |
svadhāmāni yayuḥ prītyā saṃstuvantaḥ śivaṃ śivam ||
3.7.d:
विष्ण्वादयः सुराः सर्वे प्रशंसन्तो ह्यमी तदा ।
स्वधामानि ययुः प्रीत्या संस्तुवन्तः शिवं शिवम् ॥
3.7.m: All those gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, then praising, / went gladly to their own realms, extolling the auspicious Śiva.

3.7.s:
iti te kathito vatsa svāvatāro mahāmune |
sadānandakaraḥ puṃsāṃ śivabhaktipravarddhanaḥ ||
3.7.d:
इति ते कथितो वत्स स्वावतारो महामुने ।
सदानन्दकरः पुंसां शिवभक्तिप्रवर्द्धनः ॥
3.7.m: Thus has been recounted to you, my child, my own manifestation, O great sage, / which ever bestows joy on men and increases devotion to Śiva.

3.7.s:
ya idaṃ nandino janma varadānaṃ tathā mama |
abhiṣekaṃ vivāhaṃ ca śṛṇuyācchrāvayettathā ||
3.7.d:
य इदं नन्दिनो जन्म वरदानं तथा मम ।
अभिषेकं विवाहं च शृणुयाच्छ्रावयेत्तथा ॥
3.7.m: Whoever hears or recites this birth of Nandin, / and likewise the granting of my boons, my consecration, and my marriage,

3.7.s:
paṭhedvā pāṭhayedvāpi śraddhāvānbhaktisaṃyutaḥ |
iha sarvasukhaṃ bhuktvā paratra labhate gatim ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.7.d:
पठेद्वा पाठयेद्वापि श्रद्धावान्भक्तिसंयुतः ।
इह सर्वसुखं भुक्त्वा परत्र लभते गतिम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.7.m:
or reads it, or causes it to be read, faithful and endowed with devotion, / having enjoyed every happiness here, attains the [supreme] state hereafter.'

Thus ends the seventh chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Manifestation, Consecration, and Marriage of Nandikeśvara', in the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, the third [part] of the auspicious Śiva Purāṇa.

3.8.s:
atha bhairavāvatāramāha |
nandīśvara uvāca |
sanatkumāra sarvajña śṛṇu tvaṃ bhairavīṃ kathām |
yasyāḥ śravaṇamātreṇa śaivī bhaktirdṛḍhā bhavet ||
3.8.d:
अथ भैरवावतारमाह ।
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ शृणु त्वं भैरवीं कथाम् ।
यस्याः श्रवणमात्रेण शैवी भक्तिर्दृढा भवेत् ॥
3.8.m: Now he declares the manifestation of Bhairava. / Nandīśvara said: / 'O omniscient Sanatkumāra, listen to the narrative of Bhairava, / by merely hearing which devotion to Śiva becomes firm.

3.8.s:
bhairavaḥ pūrṇarūpo hi śaṅkarasya parātmanaḥ |
mūḍhāstaṃ vai na jānanti mohitāḥ śivamāyayā ||
3.8.d:
भैरवः पूर्णरूपो हि शङ्करस्य परात्मनः ।
मूढास्तं वै न जानन्ति मोहिताः शिवमायया ॥
3.8.m: Bhairava is indeed the complete form of Śaṅkara, the supreme Self; / the deluded do not know him, bewitched by the māyā of Śiva.

3.8.s:
sanatkumāra no vetti mahimānaṃ maheśituḥ |
caturbhujo'pi viṣṇurvai caturvaktro'pi vai vidhiḥ ||
3.8.d:
सनत्कुमार नो वेत्ति महिमानं महेशितुः ।
चतुर्भुजोऽपि विष्णुर्वै चतुर्वक्त्रोऽपि वै विधिः ॥
3.8.m: Sanatkumāra, even four-armed Viṣṇu / and even four-faced Brahmā do not know the greatness of the Great Lord.

3.8.s:
citramatra na kiñcidvai durjñeyā khalu śāmbhavī |
tayā sammohitāḥ sarve nārcayantyapi taṃ param ||
3.8.d:
चित्रमत्र न किञ्चिद्वै दुर्ज्ञेया खलु शाम्भवी ।
तया सम्मोहिताः सर्वे नार्चयन्त्यपि तं परम् ॥
3.8.m: There is no wonder here at all: the [power] of Śambhu is indeed hard to understand; / deluded by it, they do not even worship that supreme [Lord].

3.8.s:
vedayedyadi vātmānaṃ sa eva parameśvaraḥ |
tadā vidanti te sarve svecchayā na hi ke'pi tam ||
3.8.d:
वेदयेद्यदि वात्मानं स एव परमेश्वरः ।
तदा विदन्ति ते सर्वे स्वेच्छया न हि केऽपि तम् ॥
3.8.m: If Parameśvara himself should make himself known, / only then do they all know him; no one [knows him] by their own will.

3.8.s:
sarvago'pi maheśāno nekṣyate mūḍhabuddhibhiḥ |
devavad budhyate loke yo'tīto manasāṃ girām ||
3.8.d:
सर्वगोऽपि महेशानो नेक्ष्यते मूढबुद्धिभिः ।
देववद् बुध्यते लोके योऽतीतो मनसां गिराम् ॥
3.8.m: Though the Great Lord is omnipresent, he is not seen by the foolish-minded; / he who is beyond minds and words is perceived in the world like [an ordinary] god.

3.8.s:
atretihāsaṃ vakṣye'haṃ paramarṣe purātanam |
śṛṇu taṃ śraddhayā tāta paramaṃ jñānakāraṇam ||
3.8.d:
अत्रेतिहासं वक्ष्येऽहं परमर्षे पुरातनम् ।
शृणु तं श्रद्धया तात परमं ज्ञानकारणम् ॥
3.8.m: In this regard I shall relate an ancient narrative, O supreme sage; / listen to it with faith, dear child, as the supreme cause of knowledge.

3.8.s:
meruśṛṅge'dbhute ramye sthitaṃ brahmāṇamīśvaram |
jagmurdevarṣayaḥ sarve sutattvaṃ jñātumicchayā ||
3.8.d:
मेरुशृङ्गेऽद्भुते रम्ये स्थितं ब्रह्माणमीश्वरम् ।
जग्मुर्देवर्षयः सर्वे सुतत्त्वं ज्ञातुमिच्छया ॥
3.8.m: To the lord Brahmā, who was seated on the wondrous, delightful peak of Meru, / all the celestial seers went with the desire to know the true reality.

3.8.s:
tatrāgatya vidhiṃ natvā papracchuste mahādarāt |
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve nataskandhā munīśvarāḥ ||
3.8.d:
तत्रागत्य विधिं नत्वा पप्रच्छुस्ते महादरात् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे नतस्कन्धा मुनीश्वराः ॥
3.8.m: Having arrived there and bowed to Brahmā, they asked with great reverence, / all those lords of sages with hands folded in supplication and shoulders bowed.

3.8.s:
devarṣaya ūcuḥ |
devadeva prajānātha sṛṣṭikṛllokanāyaka |
tattvato vada cāsmabhyaṃ kimekaṃ tattvamavyayam ||
3.8.d:
देवर्षय ऊचुः ।
देवदेव प्रजानाथ सृष्टिकृल्लोकनायक ।
तत्त्वतो वद चास्मभ्यं किमेकं तत्त्वमव्ययम् ॥
3.8.m: The celestial seers said: / "O god of gods, lord of creatures, creator of the universe, leader of the worlds! / Tell us truly, what is the one imperishable reality?"

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sa māyayā maheśasya mohitaḥ padmasambhavaḥ |
avijñāya paraṃ bhāvaṃ sambhāvaṃ pratyuvāca ha ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
स मायया महेशस्य मोहितः पद्मसम्भवः ।
अविज्ञाय परं भावं सम्भावं प्रत्युवाच ह ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Deluded by the māyā of the Great Lord, / the lotus-born [Brahmā], not knowing the supreme state, replied with self-importance:

3.8.s:
brahmovāca |
he surā ṛṣayaḥ sarve sumatyā śṛṇutādarāt |
vacmyahaṃ paramaṃ tattvamavyayaṃ vai yathārthataḥ ||
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
हे सुरा ऋषयः सर्वे सुमत्या शृणुतादरात् ।
वच्म्यहं परमं तत्त्वमव्ययं वै यथार्थतः ॥
3.8.m: Brahmā said: / "O gods, O all seers! Listen with good intellect and reverence; / I shall declare to you the supreme imperishable reality as it truly is.

3.8.s:
jagadyonirahaṃ dhātā svayambhūraja īśvaraḥ |
anādibhāgahaṃ brahma hyeka ātmā nirañjanaḥ ||
3.8.d:
जगद्योनिरहं धाता स्वयम्भूरज ईश्वरः ।
अनादिभागहं ब्रह्म ह्येक आत्मा निरञ्जनः ॥
3.8.m: I am the womb of the universe, the Creator, the self-existent, unborn Lord; / I am Brahman without beginning or end, the one untainted Self.

3.8.s:
pravartako hi jagatāmahameva nivarttakaḥ |
saṃvartako madadhiko nānyaḥ kaścitsurottamāḥ ||
3.8.d:
प्रवर्तको हि जगतामहमेव निवर्त्तकः ।
संवर्तको मदधिको नान्यः कश्चित्सुरोत्तमाः ॥
3.8.m: I alone am the originator of the worlds, the sustainer, / and the destroyer. None other is greater than I, O best of gods!"

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
tasyaivaṃ vadato dhāturviṣṇustatra sthito mune |
provāca prahasanvākyaṃ saṅkruddho mohito'jayā ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
तस्यैवं वदतो धातुर्विष्णुस्तत्र स्थितो मुने ।
प्रोवाच प्रहसन्वाक्यं सङ्क्रुद्धो मोहितोऽजया ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / 'While the Creator was speaking thus, Viṣṇu, who was standing there, O sage, / laughing aloud and enraged, deluded by the Unborn [Māyā], said:

3.8.s:
na caitaducitā brahmanyogayuktasya mūrkhatā |
avijñāya paraṃ tattvaṃ vṛthaitatte nigadyate ||
3.8.d:
न चैतदुचिता ब्रह्मन्योगयुक्तस्य मूर्खता ।
अविज्ञाय परं तत्त्वं वृथैतत्ते निगद्यते ॥
3.8.m: "This foolishness is not fitting for one endowed with yoga, O Brahman! / Not knowing the supreme reality, this is spoken in vain by you.

3.8.s:
kartā'haṃ sarvalokānāṃ paramātmā paraḥ pumān |
yajño nārāyaṇo devo māyādhīśaḥ parāgatiḥ ||
3.8.d:
कर्ताऽहं सर्वलोकानां परमात्मा परः पुमान् ।
यज्ञो नारायणो देवो मायाधीशः परागतिः ॥
3.8.m: I am the maker of all the worlds, the supreme Self, the supreme Person, / the sacrifice, the divine Nārāyaṇa, the master of māyā, the supreme refuge.

3.8.s:
mamājñayā tvayā brahman sṛṣṭireṣā vidhīyate |
jagatāṃ jīvanaṃ naiva māmanādṛtya ceśvaram ||
3.8.d:
ममाज्ञया त्वया ब्रह्मन् सृष्टिरेषा विधीयते ।
जगतां जीवनं नैव मामनादृत्य चेश्वरम् ॥
3.8.m: By my command, O Brahman, this creation is performed by you; / there is indeed no life for the worlds without honoring me, the Lord."

3.8.s:
evaṃ viprakṛtau mohātparasparajayaiṣiṇau |
procaturnigamāṃścātra pramāṇe sarvathā tanau ||
3.8.d:
एवं विप्रकृतौ मोहात्परस्परजयैषिणौ ।
प्रोचतुर्निगमांश्चात्र प्रमाणे सर्वथा तनौ ॥
3.8.m: Being thus confused by delusion, each wishing for victory over the other, / they addressed the Vedas in embodied form, [which were] authoritative in every way.

3.8.s:
praṣṭavyāste viśeṣeṇa sthitā mūrtidharāśca te |
papracchatuḥ pramāṇajñānityuktvā caturo'pi tān ||
3.8.d:
प्रष्टव्यास्ते विशेषेण स्थिता मूर्तिधराश्च ते ।
पप्रच्छतुः प्रमाणज्ञानित्युक्त्वा चतुरोऽपि तान् ॥
3.8.m: Saying, "They who stand possessing bodily forms must particularly be questioned," / the two asked all four of them who knew the authorities.

3.8.s:
vidhiviṣṇū ūcatuḥ |
vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra pratiṣṭhāṃ paramāmitāḥ |
yūyaṃ vadata viśrabdhaṃ kimekaṃ tattvamavyayam ||
3.8.d:
विधिविष्णू ऊचतुः ।
वेदाः प्रमाणं सर्वत्र प्रतिष्ठां परमामिताः ।
यूयं वदत विश्रब्धं किमेकं तत्त्वमव्ययम् ॥
3.8.m: Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: / "The Vedas are the authority everywhere, established as supreme. / Tell us with confidence, what is the one imperishable reality?"

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityākarṇya tayorvācaṃ punaste hi ṛgādayaḥ |
avadaṃstattvataḥ sarve pareśaṃ saṃsmarato prabhum ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य तयोर्वाचं पुनस्ते हि ऋगादयः ।
अवदंस्तत्त्वतः सर्वे परेशं संस्मरतो प्रभुम् ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / 'Hearing the words of the two, the [Vedas], beginning with the Ṛg, / then all spoke according to truth, meditating on the supreme Lord.'

3.8.s:
yadi mānyā vayaṃ devau sṛṣṭisthitikarau vibhū |
tadā pramāṇaṃ vakṣyāmo bhavatsandehabhedakam ||
3.8.d:
यदि मान्या वयं देवौ सृष्टिस्थितिकरौ विभू ।
तदा प्रमाणं वक्ष्यामो भवत्सन्देहभेदकम् ॥
3.8.m: "If we are respected by you two lords, the almighty agents of creation and sustenance, / then we shall state the authoritative testimony that will resolve your doubt."

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
śrutyuktavidhimākarṇya procatustau surau śrutīḥ |
yuṣmaduktaṃ pramāṇaṃ nau kiṃ tattvaṃ samyagucyatām ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
श्रुत्युक्तविधिमाकर्ण्य प्रोचतुस्तौ सुरौ श्रुतीः ।
युष्मदुक्तं प्रमाणं नौ किं तत्त्वं सम्यगुच्यताम् ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Hearing this statement of the Vedas, the two gods spoke to the Vedas: / "Your word is our authority. Let that principle be clearly stated!"

3.8.s:
ṛgveda uvāca |
yadantaḥ sthāni bhūtāni yataḥ sarvaṃ pravarttate |
yadāhuḥ paramaṃ tattvaṃ sa rudrastveka eva hi ||
3.8.d:
ऋग्वेद उवाच ।
यदन्तः स्थानि भूतानि यतः सर्वं प्रवर्त्तते ।
यदाहुः परमं तत्त्वं स रुद्रस्त्वेक एव हि ॥
3.8.m: The Ṛgveda said: / "He within whom all beings abide, from whom everything proceeds, / and whom they call the supreme principle—he alone is verily Rudra."

3.8.s:
yajurveda uvāca |
yo yajñairakhilairīśo yogena ca samijyate |
yena pramāṇaṃ khalu naḥ sa ekaḥ sarvadṛk śivaḥ ||
3.8.d:
यजुर्वेद उवाच ।
यो यज्ञैरखिलैरीशो योगेन च समिज्यते ।
येन प्रमाणं खलु नः स एकः सर्वदृक् शिवः ॥
3.8.m: The Yajurveda said: / "He who is the Lord worshipped through all sacrifices and through yoga, / by whom our authoritativeness is indeed established—he, the all-seeing, is the one Śiva."

3.8.s:
sāmaveda uvāca |
yenedaṃ bhramyate viśvaṃ yogibhiryo vicintyate |
yadbhāsā bhāsate viśvaṃ sa ekastryambakaḥ paraḥ ||
3.8.d:
सामवेद उवाच ।
येनेदं भ्रम्यते विश्वं योगिभिर्यो विचिन्त्यते ।
यद्भासा भासते विश्वं स एकस्त्र्यम्बकः परः ॥
3.8.m: The Sāmaveda said: / "He by whom this universe is revolved, who is meditated upon by yogins, / and by whose light the universe shines—he is the one supreme Tryambaka."

3.8.s:
atharvaṇaveda uvāca |
yaṃ prapaśyanti deveśaṃ bhaktyanugrahiṇo janāḥ |
tamāhurekaṃ kaivalyaṃ śaṅkaraṃ duḥkhataḥ param ||
3.8.d:
अथर्वणवेद उवाच ।
यं प्रपश्यन्ति देवेशं भक्त्यनुग्रहिणो जनाः ।
तमाहुरेकं कैवल्यं शङ्करं दुःखतः परम् ॥
3.8.m: The Atharvaveda said: / "The Lord of gods whom people behold when blessed with devotion— / him they proclaim as Śaṅkara, the one absolute liberation beyond sorrow."

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
śrutyuktamidamākarṇyātīva māyāvimohitau |
smitvāhaturvidhiharī nigamāṃstānvicetanau ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
श्रुत्युक्तमिदमाकर्ण्यातीव मायाविमोहितौ ।
स्मित्वाहतुर्विधिहरी निगमांस्तान्विचेतनौ ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Hearing what the Vedas said, thoroughly deluded by Māyā, / Brahmā and Hari smiled, deprived of good sense, and spoke to those Vedas:

3.8.s:
vidhiharī ūcatuḥ |
he vedāḥ kimidaṃ yūyaṃ bhāṣante gatacetanāḥ |
kiṃ jātaṃ vo'dya sarvaṃ hi naṣṭaṃ suvayunaṃ param ||
3.8.d:
विधिहरी ऊचतुः ।
हे वेदाः किमिदं यूयं भाषन्ते गतचेतनाः ।
किं जातं वोऽद्य सर्वं हि नष्टं सुवयुनं परम् ॥
3.8.m: Brahmā and Hari said: / "O Vedas! What is this that you speak, having lost your senses? / What has happened to you today? All your supreme knowledge has indeed vanished!

3.8.s:
kathaṃ pramathanātho'sau ramamāṇo nirantaram |
digambaraḥ pītavarṇo śivayā dhūlidhūsaraḥ ||
3.8.d:
कथं प्रमथनाथोऽसौ रममाणो निरन्तरम् ।
दिगम्बरः पीतवर्णो शिवया धूलिधूसरः ॥
3.8.m: How could this lord of Pramathas, who sports perpetually, / sky-clad, yellow-hued, grey with dust alongside his consort Śivā,

3.8.s:
virūpaveṣo jaṭilo vṛṣago vyālabhūṣaṇaḥ |
paraṃ brahmatvamāpannaḥ kva ca tatsaṅgavarjitam ||
3.8.d:
विरूपवेषो जटिलो वृषगो व्यालभूषणः ।
परं ब्रह्मत्वमापन्नः क्व च तत्सङ्गवर्जितम् ॥
3.8.m: misshapen in appearance, matted-haired, riding a bull, adorned with serpents, / have attained the status of supreme Brahman? How far removed is that [Brahman] from such attachment!"

3.8.s:
ityudīritamākarṇya praṇavaḥ sarvagastayoḥ |
amūrto mūrtimānprītyā jṛmbhamāṇa uvāca tau ||
3.8.d:
इत्युदीरितमाकर्ण्य प्रणवः सर्वगस्तयोः ।
अमूर्तो मूर्तिमान्प्रीत्या जृम्भमाण उवाच तौ ॥
3.8.m: Hearing what had been uttered by the two, the all-pervading Praṇava, / formless yet assuming a form, affectionately manifested itself and said to them:

3.8.s:
praṇava uvāca |
na hīśo bhagavān śaktyā hyātmano vyatiriktayā |
kadācidramate rudro līlārūpadharo haraḥ ||
3.8.d:
प्रणव उवाच ।
न हीशो भगवान् शक्त्या ह्यात्मनो व्यतिरिक्तया ।
कदाचिद्रमते रुद्रो लीलारूपधरो हरः ॥
3.8.m: Praṇava said: / "Never does the blessed Lord Rudra, Hara who bears sportive forms, / sport with a power distinct from his own self.

3.8.s:
asau hi parameśānaḥ svayañjyotiḥ sanātanaḥ |
ānandarūpā tasyaiṣā śaktirnāgantukī śivā ||
3.8.d:
असौ हि परमेशानः स्वयञ्ज्योतिः सनातनः ।
आनन्दरूपा तस्यैषा शक्तिर्नागन्तुकी शिवा ॥
3.8.m: Indeed, this Parameśāna is the eternal, self-luminous light; / this Śivā is his innate power consisting of bliss, not something accidental."

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityevamukto'pi tadā vidherviṣṇośca vai tadā |
nājñānamagamannāśaṃ śrīkaṇṭhasyaiva māyayā ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तोऽपि तदा विधेर्विष्णोश्च वै तदा ।
नाज्ञानमगमन्नाशं श्रीकण्ठस्यैव मायया ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Even though it was explained in this manner, then the ignorance / of Brahmā and Viṣṇu did not perish, due to the very Māyā of Śrīkaṇṭha.

3.8.s:
prādurāsīttato jyotirubhayorantare mahat |
pūrayannijayā bhāsā dyāvābhūmyoryadantaram ||
3.8.d:
प्रादुरासीत्ततो ज्योतिरुभयोरन्तरे महत् ।
पूरयन्निजया भासा द्यावाभूम्योर्यदन्तरम् ॥
3.8.m: Then between the two of them a great light became manifest, / filling with its own radiance the intermediate space between heaven and earth.

3.8.s:
jyotirmaṇḍalamadhyastho dadṛśe puruṣākṛtiḥ |
vidhikratubhyāṃ tatraiva mahādbhutatanurmune ||
3.8.d:
ज्योतिर्मण्डलमध्यस्थो ददृशे पुरुषाकृतिः ।
विधिक्रतुभ्यां तत्रैव महाद्भुततनुर्मुने ॥
3.8.m: Standing in the midst of that mass of light, a form of a man / with a wondrous body was seen right there, O sage, by Brahmā and Viṣṇu.

3.8.s:
prajajvālātha kopena brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ |
āvayorantare ko'sau bibhṛyātpuruṣākṛtim ||
3.8.d:
प्रजज्वालाथ कोपेन ब्रह्मणः पञ्चमं शिरः ।
आवयोरन्तरे कोऽसौ बिभृयात्पुरुषाकृतिम् ॥
3.8.m: Thereupon the fifth head of Brahmā blazed with wrath: / "Who is this that assumes a human form between the two of us?"

3.8.s:
vidhiḥ sambhāvayedyāvattāvatsa trivilocanaḥ |
dṛṣṭaḥ kṣaṇena ca mahāpuruṣo nīlalohitaḥ ||
3.8.d:
विधिः सम्भावयेद्यावत्तावत्स त्रिविलोचनः ।
दृष्टः क्षणेन च महापुरुषो नीललोहितः ॥
3.8.m: While Brahmā was still conjecturing, within a moment that three-eyed / great being, the dark and red Nīlalohita, was seen:

3.8.s:
triśūlapāṇirbhālākṣo nāgoḍupavibhūṣaṇaḥ |
hiraṇyagarbhastaṃ dṛṣṭvā vihasanprāha mohitaḥ ||
3.8.d:
त्रिशूलपाणिर्भालाक्षो नागोडुपविभूषणः ।
हिरण्यगर्भस्तं दृष्ट्वा विहसन्प्राह मोहितः ॥
3.8.m: holding a trident in his hand, with an eye on his forehead, adorned with a snake and the crescent moon. / Seeing him, Hiraṇyagarbha, utterly deluded, laughed and said:

3.8.s:
brahmovāca |
nīlalohita jāne tvāṃ mā bhaiṣīścandraśekhara |
bhālasthalānmama purā rudraḥ prādurabhūdbhavān ||
3.8.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
नीललोहित जाने त्वां मा भैषीश्चन्द्रशेखर ।
भालस्थलान्मम पुरा रुद्रः प्रादुरभूद्भवान् ॥
3.8.m: Brahmā said: / "Nīlalohita, I know you! Do not be afraid, O Candraśekhara! / Formerly, you appeared as Rudra from my forehead.

3.8.s:
rodanād rudranāmāpi yojito'si mayā purā |
māmeva śaraṇaṃ yāhi putra rakṣāṃ karomi te ||
3.8.d:
रोदनाद् रुद्रनामापि योजितोऽसि मया पुरा ।
मामेव शरणं याहि पुत्र रक्षां करोमि ते ॥
3.8.m: Because you wept, the name 'Rudra' was given to you by me in the past. / Seek refuge in me alone, my son; I shall protect you!"

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
atheśvaraḥ padmayoneḥ śrutvā garvavatīṃ giram |
cukopātīva ca tadā kurvanniva layammune ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
अथेश्वरः पद्मयोनेः श्रुत्वा गर्ववतीं गिरम् ।
चुकोपातीव च तदा कुर्वन्निव लयम्मुने ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Then, hearing the arrogant speech of the lotus-born [Brahmā], Īśvara / became exceedingly enraged at that time, O sage, as if causing cosmic dissolution.

3.8.s:
sa kopataḥ samutpādya puruṣaṃ bhairavaṃ kvacit |
prajvalantaṃ sumahasā prītyā ca parameśvaraḥ ||
3.8.d:
स कोपतः समुत्पाद्य पुरुषं भैरवं क्वचित् ।
प्रज्वलन्तं सुमहसा प्रीत्या च परमेश्वरः ॥
3.8.m: From his wrath, Parameśvara brought forth somewhere a terrible being, Bhairava, / blazing with immense splendour, and out of affection [spoke to him].

3.8.s:
īśvara uvāca |
prāk ca paṅkajajanmāsau śāsyaste kālabhairava |
kālavadrājase sākṣātkālarājastato bhavān ||
3.8.d:
ईश्वर उवाच ।
प्राक् च पङ्कजजन्मासौ शास्यस्ते कालभैरव ।
कालवद्राजसे साक्षात्कालराजस्ततो भवान् ॥
3.8.m: Īśvara said: / "First, this lotus-born one is to be chastised by you, O Kālabhairava! / You shine forth like time, death, itself in visible form; therefore you are Kālarāja.

3.8.s:
viśvaṃ bharttuṃ samartho'si bhīṣaṇādbhairavaḥ smṛtaḥ |
tvatto bheṣyati kālo'pi tatastvaṃ kālabhairavaḥ ||
3.8.d:
विश्वं भर्त्तुं समर्थोऽसि भीषणाद्भैरवः स्मृतः ।
त्वत्तो भेष्यति कालोऽपि ततस्त्वं कालभैरवः ॥
3.8.m: You are capable of sustaining the universe, and because of your terrifying nature you are called Bhairava; / even Time/Death will fear you, and hence you are Kālabhairava.

3.8.s:
āmardayiṣyati bhavānruṣṭo duṣṭātmano yataḥ |
āmardaka iti khyātiṃ tataḥ sarvatra yāsyasi ||
3.8.d:
आमर्दयिष्यति भवान्रुष्टो दुष्टात्मनो यतः ।
आमर्दक इति ख्यातिं ततः सर्वत्र यास्यसि ॥
3.8.m: Because you will crush the wicked when enraged, / you will therefore attain fame everywhere under the name Āmardaka.

3.8.s:
yataḥ pāpāni bhaktānāṃ bhakṣayiṣyasi tatkṣaṇāt |
pāpabhakṣaṇa ityeva tava nāma bhaviṣyati ||
3.8.d:
यतः पापानि भक्तानां भक्षयिष्यसि तत्क्षणात् ।
पापभक्षण इत्येव तव नाम भविष्यति ॥
3.8.m: Because you will devour the sins of devotees instantly, / your name will therefore be Pāpabhakṣaṇa.

3.8.s:
yā me muktipurī kāśī sarvābhyo'pi garīyasī |
ādhipatyaṃ ca tasyāste kālarāja sadaiva hi ||
3.8.d:
या मे मुक्तिपुरी काशी सर्वाभ्योऽपि गरीयसी ।
आधिपत्यं च तस्यास्ते कालराज सदैव हि ॥
3.8.m: My city of liberation, Kāśī, is greater than all others, / and the lordship over it shall be yours forever, O Kālarāja.

3.8.s:
tatra ye pātakinarāsteṣāṃ śāstā tvameva hi |
śubhāśubhaṃ ca tatkarma citragupto likhiṣyati ||
3.8.d:
तत्र ये पातकिनरास्तेषां शास्ता त्वमेव हि ।
शुभाशुभं च तत्कर्म चित्रगुप्तो लिखिष्यति ॥
3.8.m: You alone shall be the chastiser of the sinful men there, / and Citragupta will record their good and evil deeds."

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
etānvarānpragṛhyātha tatkṣaṇātkālabhairavaḥ |
vāmāṅgulinakhāgreṇa cakarta ca vidheśśiraḥ ||
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एतान्वरान्प्रगृह्याथ तत्क्षणात्कालभैरवः ।
वामाङ्गुलिनखाग्रेण चकर्त च विधेश्शिरः ॥
3.8.m: Nandīśvara said: / Then, having received these boons, Kālabhairava instantly / severed Brahmā's head with the tip of the nail of his left finger.

3.8.s:
yadaṅgamaparādhnoti kāryaṃ tasyaiva śāsanam |
ato yena kṛtā nindā tacchinnaṃ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ ||
3.8.d:
यदङ्गमपराध्नोति कार्यं तस्यैव शासनम् ।
अतो येन कृता निन्दा तच्छिन्नं पञ्चमं शिरः ॥
3.8.m: The limb that commits an offense is the very one to be punished; / therefore, the fifth head, by which the insult was uttered, was severed.

3.8.s:
atha chinnaṃ vidhiśiro dṛṣṭvā bhītataro hariḥ |
śātarudriyamantraiśca bhaktyā tuṣṭāva śaṅkaram ||
3.8.d:
अथ छिन्नं विधिशिरो दृष्ट्वा भीततरो हरिः ।
शातरुद्रियमन्त्रैश्च भक्त्या तुष्टाव शङ्करम् ॥
3.8.m: Then, seeing Brahmā's severed head, Hari became extremely terrified, / and with devotion he praised Śaṅkara with the hymns of the Śatarudriya.

3.8.s:
bhīto hiraṇyagarbho'pi jajāpa śatarudriyam |
itthaṃ tau gatagarvau hi sañjātau tatkṣaṇānmune ||
3.8.d:
भीतो हिरण्यगर्भोऽपि जजाप शतरुद्रियम् ।
इत्थं तौ गतगर्वौ हि सञ्जातौ तत्क्षणान्मुने ॥
3.8.m: Terrified, Hiraṇyagarbha too chanted the Śatarudriya. / Thus, O sage, the two were instantly stripped of their pride.

3.8.s:
parabrahma śivaḥ sākṣātsaccidānandalakṣaṇaḥ |
paramātmā guṇātīta iti jñānamavāpatuḥ ||
3.8.d:
परब्रह्म शिवः साक्षात्सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणः ।
परमात्मा गुणातीत इति ज्ञानमवापतुः ॥
3.8.m: They attained the knowledge that Śiva is directly the supreme Brahman, / characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss, the supreme self beyond the qualities.

3.8.s:
sanatkumāra sarvajña śṛṇu me paramaṃ śubham |
yāvadgarvo bhavettāvajjñānaguptirviśeṣataḥ ||
3.8.d:
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ शृणु मे परमं शुभम् ।
यावद्गर्वो भवेत्तावज्ज्ञानगुप्तिर्विशेषतः ॥
3.8.m: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, hear from me this most auspicious truth: / as long as pride exists, to that extent true knowledge remains hidden.

3.8.s:
tyaktvābhimānaṃ puruṣo jānāti parameśvaram |
garviṇaṃ hanti viśveśo jāto garvāpahārakaḥ ||
3.8.d:
त्यक्त्वाभिमानं पुरुषो जानाति परमेश्वरम् ।
गर्विणं हन्ति विश्वेशो जातो गर्वापहारकः ॥
3.8.m: Having cast off egoism, a man knows Parameśvara. / The Lord of the universe destroys the proud; he is born as the remover of pride.

3.8.s:
atha viṣṇuvidhī jñātvā vigarvau parameśvaraḥ |
prasanno'bhūnmahādevo'karottāvabhayau prabhuḥ ||
3.8.d:
अथ विष्णुविधी ज्ञात्वा विगर्वौ परमेश्वरः ।
प्रसन्नोऽभून्महादेवोऽकरोत्तावभयौ प्रभुः ॥
3.8.m: Then, seeing Viṣṇu and Brahmā free from pride, Parameśvara, / the lord Mahādeva, was pleased and granted them freedom from fear.

3.8.s:
āśvāsya tau mahādevaḥ prītaḥ praṇatavatsalaḥ |
prāha svāṃ mūrtimaparāṃ bhairavantaṃ kaparddinam ||
3.8.d:
आश्वास्य तौ महादेवः प्रीतः प्रणतवत्सलः ।
प्राह स्वां मूर्तिमपरां भैरवन्तं कपर्द्दिनम् ॥
3.8.m: Having consoled the two, Mahādeva, delighted and affectionate toward the surrendered, / spoke to his other form, that Bhairava with matted hair:

3.8.s:
mahādeva uvāca |
tvayā mānyo viṣṇurasau tathā śatadhṛtiḥ svayam |
kapālaṃ vaidhasaṃ vāpi nīlalohita dhāraya ||
3.8.d:
महादेव उवाच ।
त्वया मान्यो विष्णुरसौ तथा शतधृतिः स्वयम् ।
कपालं वैधसं वापि नीललोहित धारय ॥
3.8.m: Mahādeva said: / "You must respect this Viṣṇu, and likewise Brahmā himself. / O Nīlalohita, take up this skull of Brahmā.

3.8.s:
brahmahatyāpanodāya vrataṃ lokāya darśaya |
cara tvaṃ satataṃ bhikṣāṃ kapālavratamāśritaḥ ||
3.8.d:
ब्रह्महत्यापनोदाय व्रतं लोकाय दर्शय ।
चर त्वं सततं भिक्षां कपालव्रतमाश्रितः ॥
3.8.m: To demonstrate the expiation of brahminicide to the world, show them the rite; / wander continuously for alms, adhering to the observance of the skull."

3.8.s:
ityuktvā paśyatastasya tejorūpaḥ śivo'bravīt |
utpādya caikāṃ kanyāṃ tu brahmahatyābhiviśrutām ||
3.8.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पश्यतस्तस्य तेजोरूपः शिवोऽब्रवीत् ।
उत्पाद्य चैकां कन्यां तु ब्रह्महत्याभिविश्रुताम् ॥
3.8.m: Having spoken thus while he looked on, Śiva, who is of the form of light, spoke, / having generated a maiden renowned as Brahmahatyā:

3.8.s:
yāvadvārāṇasīṃ divyāṃ purīmeṣāṃ gamiṣyati |
tāvattvaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ kālamanugacchograrūpiṇam ||
3.8.d:
यावद्वाराणसीं दिव्यां पुरीमेषां गमिष्यति ।
तावत्त्वं भीषणं कालमनुगच्छोग्ररूपिणम् ॥
3.8.m: Until he reaches this divine city of Vārāṇasī, / do you follow this terrible, fierce-formed Kāla.

3.8.s:
sarvatra te praveśo'sti tyaktvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm |
vārāṇasīṃ yadā gacchettanmukto bhava tatkṣaṇāt ||
3.8.d:
सर्वत्र ते प्रवेशोऽस्ति त्यक्त्वा वाराणसीं पुरीम् ।
वाराणसीं यदा गच्छेत्तन्मुक्तो भव तत्क्षणात् ॥
3.8.m: You have access everywhere, except the city of Vārāṇasī; / when he enters Vārāṇasī, become freed from that instantly."

3.8.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
niyojya tāmiti tadā brahmahatyāṃ ca tāṃ prabhuḥ |
mahādbhutaśca sa śivo'pyantardhānamagāttataḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.8.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
नियोज्य तामिति तदा ब्रह्महत्यां च तां प्रभुः ।
महाद्भुतश्च स शिवोऽप्यन्तर्धानमगात्ततः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.8.m:
Nandīśvara said: / Having thus assigned that Brahmahatyā at that time, / that wonderful lord Śiva then vanished from sight.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Incarnation of Bhairava,' in the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, the third section of the glorious Śivapurāṇa.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sanatkumāra sarvajña bhairavīmaparāṃ kathām |
śṛṇu prītyā mahādoṣasaṃhartrīṃ bhaktivarddhinīm ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ भैरवीमपरां कथाम् ।
शृणु प्रीत्या महादोषसंहर्त्रीं भक्तिवर्द्धिनीम् ॥
3.9.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Omniscient Sanatkumāra, listen with joy to another story of Bhairava, / which destroys great sins and increases devotion.

3.9.s:
tatsānnidhyaṃ bhairavo'pi kālo'bhūtkālakālanaḥ |
sa devadevavākyena bibhratkāpālikaṃ vratam ||
3.9.d:
तत्सान्निध्यं भैरवोऽपि कालोऽभूत्कालकालनः ।
स देवदेववाक्येन बिभ्रत्कापालिकं व्रतम् ॥
3.9.m: Remaining in his presence, Bhairava also became Kāla, who drives Time; / by the word of the God of gods, he undertook the observance of the skull-bearer.

3.9.s:
kapālapāṇirviśvātmā cacāra bhuvanatrayam |
nātyākṣīccāpi taṃ devaṃ brahmahatyāpi dāruṇā ||
3.9.d:
कपालपाणिर्विश्वात्मा चचार भुवनत्रयम् ।
नात्याक्षीच्चापि तं देवं ब्रह्महत्यापि दारुणा ॥
3.9.m: With a skull in his hand, the Soul of the universe wandered the three worlds; / nor did that terrible brahminicide leave that god.

3.9.s:
pratitīrthaṃ bhraman nāpi vimukto brahmahatyayā |
ataḥ kāmārimahimā sarvo'pi hyavagamyatām ||
3.9.d:
प्रतितीर्थं भ्रमन् नापि विमुक्तो ब्रह्महत्यया ।
अतः कामारिमहिमा सर्वोऽपि ह्यवगम्यताम् ॥
3.9.m: Though he wandered from sacred bath to sacred bath, he was not freed from the brahminicide; / therefore let the entire majesty of the Enemy of Kāma be understood!

3.9.s:
pramathaiḥ sevyamāno'pi hyekadā viharanharaḥ |
kāpāliko yayau svairī nārāyaṇaniketanam ||
3.9.d:
प्रमथैः सेव्यमानोऽपि ह्येकदा विहरन्हरः ।
कापालिको ययौ स्वैरी नारायणनिकेतनम् ॥
3.9.m: Once, while wandering about though attended by the Pramathas, / Hara, roaming at will as a skull-bearer, went to the abode of Nārāyaṇa.

3.9.s:
athāyāntaṃ mahākālaṃ trinetraṃ sarpakuṇḍalam |
mahādevāṃśasambhūtaṃ pūrṇākāraṃ ca bhairavam ||
3.9.d:
अथायान्तं महाकालं त्रिनेत्रं सर्पकुण्डलम् ।
महादेवांशसम्भूतं पूर्णाकारं च भैरवम् ॥
3.9.m: Then, seeing Mahākāla approaching, three-eyed, with serpent earrings, / born as a portion of Mahādeva, Bhairava in full form,

3.9.s:
papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau taṃ dṛṣṭvā garuḍadhvajaḥ |
devāśca munayaścaiva devanāryyaḥ samantataḥ ||
3.9.d:
पपात दण्डवद्भूमौ तं दृष्ट्वा गरुडध्वजः ।
देवाश्च मुनयश्चैव देवनार्य्यः समन्ततः ॥
3.9.m: he whose banner bears Garuḍa fell to the ground like a staff upon seeing him, / and so did the gods, the sages, and the celestial women all around.

3.9.s:
atha viṣṇuḥ praṇamyainaṃ prayātaḥ kamalāpatiḥ |
śirasyañjalimādhāya tuṣṭāva vividhaiḥ stavaiḥ ||
3.9.d:
अथ विष्णुः प्रणम्यैनं प्रयातः कमलापतिः ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय तुष्टाव विविधैः स्तवैः ॥
3.9.m: Then Viṣṇu, the husband of Kamalā, having bowed down, advanced toward him, / and, placing his folded hands upon his head, praised him with diverse hymns.

3.9.s:
sānando'tha hariḥ prāha prasannātmā mahāmune |
kṣīrodamathanodbhūtāṃ padmāṃ padmālayāṃ mudā ||
3.9.d:
सानन्दोऽथ हरिः प्राह प्रसन्नात्मा महामुने ।
क्षीरोदमथनोद्भूतां पद्मां पद्मालयां मुदा ॥
3.9.m: Then Hari, joyous and serene of soul, O great sage, / spoke gladly to Padmā, whose abode is the lotus, born from the churning of the milk ocean.

3.9.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
priye paśyābjanayane dhanyāsi subhage'naghe |
dhanyo'haṃ devi suśroṇi yatpaśyāvo jagatpatim ||
3.9.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
प्रिये पश्याब्जनयने धन्यासि सुभगेऽनघे ।
धन्योऽहं देवि सुश्रोणि यत्पश्यावो जगत्पतिम् ॥
3.9.m:
Viṣṇu said:
Look, my beloved lotus-eyed one! You are blessed, fortunate, and sinless; / I too am blessed, O goddess of beautiful hips, since we behold the Lord of the world.

3.9.s:
ayaṃ dhātā vidhātā ca lokānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ |
anādiḥ śaraṇaḥ śāntaḥ puraḥ ṣaḍviṃśasammitaḥ ||
3.9.d:
अयं धाता विधाता च लोकानां प्रभुरीश्वरः ।
अनादिः शरणः शान्तः पुरः षड्विंशसम्मितः ॥
3.9.m: He is the Creator and the Disposer, the Sovereign and the Lord of the worlds, / beginningless, the refuge, peaceful, standing before us, known as the twenty-sixth.

3.9.s:
sarvajñaḥ sarvayogīśaḥ sarvabhūtaikanāyakaḥ |
sarvabhūtāntarātmā'yaṃ sarveṣāṃ sarvadaḥ sadā ||
3.9.d:
सर्वज्ञः सर्वयोगीशः सर्वभूतैकनायकः ।
सर्वभूतान्तरात्माऽयं सर्वेषां सर्वदः सदा ॥
3.9.m: Omniscient, lord of all yogins, sole leader of all beings, / he is the inner soul of all beings, who always bestows everything upon everyone.

3.9.s:
ye vinidrā viniḥśvāsāḥ śāntāḥ dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ |
dhiyā paśyanti hṛdaye so'yaṃ padme samīkṣatām ||
3.9.d:
ये विनिद्रा विनिःश्वासाः शान्ताः ध्यानपरायणाः ।
धिया पश्यन्ति हृदये सोऽयं पद्मे समीक्षताम् ॥
3.9.m: He whom the sleepless, the breathless, the peaceful, devoted to meditation / behold in their heart by means of intellect—behold him, O Padmā!

3.9.s:
yaṃ vidurvedatattvajñā yogino yatamānasāḥ |
arūpo rūpavānbhūtvā so'yamāyāti sarvagaḥ ||
3.9.d:
यं विदुर्वेदतत्त्वज्ञा योगिनो यतमानसाः ।
अरूपो रूपवान्भूत्वा सोऽयमायाति सर्वगः ॥
3.9.m: He whom the knowers of the truth of the Veda and yogins of restrained mind know, / formless, having assumed a form, this omnipresent one arrives.

3.9.s:
aho vicitraṃ devasya ceṣṭitaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ |
yasyākhyāṃ bruvato nityaṃ na dehaḥ so'pi dehabhṛt ||
3.9.d:
अहो विचित्रं देवस्य चेष्टितं परमेष्ठिनः ।
यस्याख्यां ब्रुवतो नित्यं न देहः सोऽपि देहभृत् ॥
3.9.m: Oh, wondrous is the deed of the divine Supreme Lord! / He whose name being uttered constantly frees one from embodiment, even he has taken a body.

3.9.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā na punarjanma labhyate mānavairbhuvi |
so'yamāyāti bhagavāṃstryambakaḥ śaśibhūṣaṇaḥ ||
3.9.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा न पुनर्जन्म लभ्यते मानवैर्भुवि ।
सोऽयमायाति भगवांस्त्र्यम्बकः शशिभूषणः ॥
3.9.m: Having seen him, mortals on earth attain no rebirth; / this blessed Tryambaka arrives, adorned with the moon.

3.9.s:
puṇḍarīkadalāyāme dhanye me'dya vilocane |
yad dṛśyate mahādevo hyābhyāṃ lakṣmi maheśvaraḥ ||
3.9.d:
पुण्डरीकदलायामे धन्ये मेऽद्य विलोचने ।
यद् दृश्यते महादेवो ह्याभ्यां लक्ष्मि महेश्वरः ॥
3.9.m: Blessed today are my eyes, wide as lotus petals, / since through them Mahādeva, Maheśvara, is seen, O Lakṣmī!

3.9.s:
dhigdhikpadaṃ tu devānāṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā na śaṅkaram |
labhyate yatra nirvāṇaṃ sarvaduḥkhāntakṛttu yat ||
3.9.d:
धिग्धिक्पदं तु देवानां परं दृष्ट्वा न शङ्करम् ।
लभ्यते यत्र निर्वाणं सर्वदुःखान्तकृत्तु यत् ॥
3.9.m: Shame, shame on the rank of the gods, if after seeing the supreme Śaṅkara / liberation is not attained, which brings an end to all sorrow!

3.9.s:
devatvādaśubhaṃ kiñciddevaloke na vidyate |
dṛṣṭvāpi sarve deveśaṃ yanmuktiṃ na labhāmahe ||
3.9.d:
देवत्वादशुभं किञ्चिद्देवलोके न विद्यते ।
दृष्ट्वापि सर्वे देवेशं यन्मुक्तिं न लभामहे ॥
3.9.m: There is nothing more inauspicious in the world of the gods than divinity itself, / since even after seeing the Lord of gods, we all do not attain liberation.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ samprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ |
praṇipatya mahādevamidamāha vṛṣadhvajam ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः ।
प्रणिपत्य महादेवमिदमाह वृषध्वजम् ॥
3.9.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa, his body hairs bristling with joy, / bowed down to Mahādeva, whose banner bears the bull, and said this:

3.9.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
kimidaṃ devadevena sarvajñena tvayā vibho |
kriyate jagatāṃ dhātrā sarvapāpaharāvyaya ||
3.9.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
किमिदं देवदेवेन सर्वज्ञेन त्वया विभो ।
क्रियते जगतां धात्रा सर्वपापहराव्यय ॥
3.9.m:
Viṣṇu said:
What is this being done by you, the God of gods, the omniscient, O Lord, / the creator of the worlds, O imperishable remover of all sins?

3.9.s:
krīḍeyaṃ tava deveśa trilocana mahāmate |
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ virūpākṣa ceṣṭitaṃ te smarārdana ||
3.9.d:
क्रीडेयं तव देवेश त्रिलोचन महामते ।
किं कारणं विरूपाक्ष चेष्टितं ते स्मरार्दन ॥
3.9.m: This is a play of yours, O Lord of gods, three-eyed one of great intellect; / what is the reason, O Virūpākṣa, for this deed of yours, O crusher of Smara?

3.9.s:
kimarthaṃ bhagavañchambho bhikṣāṃ carasi śaktipa |
saṃśayo me jagannātha eṣa trailokyarājyada ||
3.9.d:
किमर्थं भगवञ्छम्भो भिक्षां चरसि शक्तिप ।
संशयो मे जगन्नाथ एष त्रैलोक्यराज्यद ॥
3.9.m: For what reason, O blessed Śambhu, keeper of the Śakti, do you wander for alms? / This doubt arises in me, O Lord of the universe, giver of the kingdom of the three worlds.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
evamuktastataḥ śambhurviṣṇunā bhairavo haraḥ |
pratyuvācādbhutotiḥ sa viṣṇuṃ hi vihasanprabhuḥ ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एवमुक्तस्ततः शम्भुर्विष्णुना भैरवो हरः ।
प्रत्युवाचाद्भुतोतिः स विष्णुं हि विहसन्प्रभुः ॥
3.9.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Addressed thus by Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Bhairava, Hara, / that lord of wondrous speech smiled and answered Viṣṇu:

3.9.s:
bhairava uvāca |
brahmaṇastu śiraśchinnamaṅgulyāgranakhena ha |
tadaghaṃ pratihantuṃ hi carāmyetad vrataṃ śubham ||
3.9.d:
भैरव उवाच ।
ब्रह्मणस्तु शिरश्छिन्नमङ्गुल्याग्रनखेन ह ।
तदघं प्रतिहन्तुं हि चराम्येतद् व्रतं शुभम् ॥
3.9.m:
Bhairava said:
The head of Brahmā was severed by the nail at the tip of my finger; / indeed, to strike down that sin I observe this auspicious rite.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
evamukto maheśena bhairaveṇa ramāpatiḥ |
smṛtvā kiñcinnataśirāḥ punarevamajijñapat ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एवमुक्तो महेशेन भैरवेण रमापतिः ।
स्मृत्वा किञ्चिन्नतशिराः पुनरेवमजिज्ञपत् ॥
3.9.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Addressed thus by the great lord Bhairava, the husband of Ramā / recalled something, bowed his head, and again addressed him thus:

3.9.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
yathecchasi tathā krīḍa sarvavighnāpanodaka |
māyayā māṃ mahādeva nācchādayitumarhasi ||
3.9.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
यथेच्छसि तथा क्रीड सर्वविघ्नापनोदक ।
मायया मां महादेव नाच्छादयितुमर्हसि ॥
3.9.m:
Viṣṇu said:
Play as you please, O dispeller of all obstacles! / You ought not to conceal me with your illusion, O Mahādeva.

3.9.s:
nābhīkamalakośāttu koṭiśaḥ kamalāsanāḥ |
kalpe kalpe purā hyānsastvanniyogabalādvibho ||
3.9.d:
नाभीकमलकोशात्तु कोटिशः कमलासनाः ।
कल्पे कल्पे पुरा ह्यान्सस्त्वन्नियोगबलाद्विभो ॥
3.9.m: For tens of millions of lotus-seated [Brahmās] came forth from the sheath of my navel-lotus / in aeon after aeon in the past, O Lord, through the power of your command.

3.9.s:
tyaja māyāmimāṃ deva dustarāmakṛtātmabhiḥ |
brahmādayo mahādeva māyayā tava mohitāḥ ||
3.9.d:
त्यज मायामिमां देव दुस्तरामकृतात्मभिः ।
ब्रह्मादयो महादेव मायया तव मोहिताः ॥
3.9.m: Cast off this illusion, O God, hard to cross for the undisciplined; / Brahmā and the others, O Mahādeva, are deluded by your illusion.

3.9.s:
yathāvadanugacchāmi ceṣṭitaṃ te śivāpate |
tavaivānugrahācchambho sarveśvara satāṅgate ||
3.9.d:
यथावदनुगच्छामि चेष्टितं ते शिवापते ।
तवैवानुग्रहाच्छम्भो सर्वेश्वर सताङ्गते ॥
3.9.m: I understand your deed properly, O Lord of Śivā, / solely by your grace, O Śambhu, Lord of all, refuge of the good.

3.9.s:
saṃhārakāle samprāpte sadevānnikhilānmunīn |
lokānvarṇāśramavato hariṣyasi yadā hara ||
3.9.d:
संहारकाले सम्प्राप्ते सदेवान्निखिलान्मुनीन् ।
लोकान्वर्णाश्रमवतो हरिष्यसि यदा हर ॥
3.9.m: When the time of dissolution arrives, having gods along with all the sages, / the worlds, endowed with social classes and stages of life, you will take away, O Hara.

3.9.s:
tadā kṛte mahādeva pāpaṃ brahmavadhādikam |
pāratantryaṃ na te śambho svairaṃ krīḍatyato bhavān ||
3.9.d:
तदा कृते महादेव पापं ब्रह्मवधादिकम् ।
पारतन्त्र्यं न ते शम्भो स्वैरं क्रीडत्यतो भवान् ॥
3.9.m: When that is done, O Mahādeva, what is the sin of killing a Brahmin and the like? / There is no subservience for you, O Śambhu, and therefore you play at your own will.

3.9.s:
atīta brahmaṇāṃ hyasthnāṃ srakkaṇṭhe tava bhāsate |
tathāpyanugatā śambho brahmahatyā tavānagha ||
3.9.d:
अतीत ब्रह्मणां ह्यस्थ्नां स्रक्कण्ठे तव भासते ।
तथाप्यनुगता शम्भो ब्रह्महत्या तवानघ ॥
3.9.m: A garland of the bones of past Brahmās shines upon your neck; / nevertheless, brahminicide pursues you, O sinless Śambhu!

3.9.s:
kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ yastvāṃ smarati mānavaḥ |
ādhāraṃ jagatāmīśa tasya pāpaṃ vilīyate ||
3.9.d:
कृत्वापि सुमहत्पापं यस्त्वां स्मरति मानवः ।
आधारं जगतामीश तस्य पापं विलीयते ॥
3.9.m: Even having committed a very great sin, the mortal who remembers you, / the foundation of the worlds, O Lord, has his sin dissolved.

3.9.s:
yathā tamo na tiṣṭheta sannidhāvaṃśumālinaḥ |
tathaiva tava yo bhaktaḥ pāpaṃ tasya vrajetkṣayam ||
3.9.d:
यथा तमो न तिष्ठेत सन्निधावंशुमालिनः ।
तथैव तव यो भक्तः पापं तस्य व्रजेत्क्षयम् ॥
3.9.m: Just as darkness cannot remain in the presence of the sun, / just so the sin of him who is devoted to you goes to destruction.

3.9.s:
yaścintayati puṇyātmā tava pādāmbujadvayam |
brahmahatyākṛtamapi pāpaṃ tasya vrajetkṣayam ||
3.9.d:
यश्चिन्तयति पुण्यात्मा तव पादाम्बुजद्वयम् ।
ब्रह्महत्याकृतमपि पापं तस्य व्रजेत्क्षयम् ॥
3.9.m: The virtuous soul who meditates upon your two lotus feet, / even his sin incurred by brahminicide goes to destruction.

3.9.s:
tava nāmānuraktā vāgyasya puṃso jagatpate |
apyadrikūṭatulitaṃ nainastamanubādhate ||
3.9.d:
तव नामानुरक्ता वाग्यस्य पुंसो जगत्पते ।
अप्यद्रिकूटतुलितं नैनस्तमनुबाधते ॥
3.9.m: That man whose speech is attached to your name, O Lord of the universe, / sin, even if equal to a mountain peak, does not torment him.

3.9.s:
paramātmanparaṃ dhāma svecchābhidhṛtavigraha |
kutūhalaṃ taveśedaṃ kṛpaṇādhīnateśvara ||
3.9.d:
परमात्मन्परं धाम स्वेच्छाभिधृतविग्रह ।
कुतूहलं तवेशेदं कृपणाधीनतेश्वर ॥
3.9.m: O Supreme Self, supreme abode, you who have assumed a body by your own will! / This curiosity is yours, O Lord, who are sovereign over those in distress.

3.9.s:
adya dhanyo'smi deveśa yanna paśyanti yoginaḥ |
paśyāmi taṃ jaganmūrttiṃ parameśvaramavyayam ||
3.9.d:
अद्य धन्योऽस्मि देवेश यन्न पश्यन्ति योगिनः ।
पश्यामि तं जगन्मूर्त्तिं परमेश्वरमव्ययम् ॥
3.9.m: Today I am blessed, O Lord of gods; he whom yogins do not behold, / that imperishable Parameśvara, whose form is the universe, I behold.

3.9.s:
adya me paramo lābhastvadya me maṅgalaṃ param |
taṃ dṛṣṭvāmṛtatṛptasya tṛṇaṃ svargāpavargakam ||
3.9.d:
अद्य मे परमो लाभस्त्वद्य मे मङ्गलं परम् ।
तं दृष्ट्वामृततृप्तस्य तृणं स्वर्गापवर्गकम् ॥
3.9.m: Today is my greatest gain, today is my supreme good fortune; / having seen him, heaven and liberation are like a blade of grass to one satisfied by nectar.

3.9.s:
itthaṃ vadati govinde vimalā padmayā tayā |
manorathavatī nāma bhikṣā pātre samarpitā ||
3.9.d:
इत्थं वदति गोविन्दे विमला पद्मया तया ।
मनोरथवती नाम भिक्षा पात्रे समर्पिता ॥
3.9.m: While Govinda was speaking thus, a pure [gift of] alms named Manorathavatī / was placed into his bowl by that Padmā.

3.9.s:
bhikṣāṭanāya devo'pi niragātparayā mudā |
anyatrāpi mahādevo bhairavaścāttavigrahaḥ ||
3.9.d:
भिक्षाटनाय देवोऽपि निरगात्परया मुदा ।
अन्यत्रापि महादेवो भैरवश्चात्तविग्रहः ॥
3.9.m: Then the god went out with supreme joy to wander for alms elsewhere as well, / Mahādeva, Bhairava, having assumed that form.

3.9.s:
dṛṣṭvānuyāyinīṃ tāṃ tu samāhūya janārdanaḥ |
samprārthayad brahmahatyāṃ vimuñca tvaṃ triśūlinam ||
3.9.d:
दृष्ट्वानुयायिनीं तां तु समाहूय जनार्दनः ।
सम्प्रार्थयद् ब्रह्महत्यां विमुञ्च त्वं त्रिशूलिनम् ॥
3.9.m: Seeing her pursuing him, however, Janārdana called her / and entreated Brahminicide: “Release the Wielder of the trident!”

3.9.s:
brahmahatyovāca |
anenāpi miṣeṇāhaṃ saṃsevyāmuṃ vṛṣadhvajam |
ātmānaṃ pāvayiṣyāmi tvapunarbhavadarśanam ||
3.9.d:
ब्रह्महत्योवाच ।
अनेनापि मिषेणाहं संसेव्यामुं वृषध्वजम् ।
आत्मानं पावयिष्यामि त्वपुनर्भवदर्शनम् ॥
3.9.m:
Brahminicide said:
Even under this pretext, by serving this one whose banner bears the bull, / I shall purify myself, the sight of whom prevents rebirth.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sā tatyāja na tatpārśvaṃ vyāhṛtāpi murāriṇā |
tamūce'tha hariṃ śambhuḥ smerāsyo bhairavo vacaḥ ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सा तत्याज न तत्पार्श्वं व्याहृतापि मुरारिणा ।
तमूचेऽथ हरिं शम्भुः स्मेरास्यो भैरवो वचः ॥
3.9.m:
Nandīśvara said:
Though addressed by Murāri, she did not leave his side; / then Śambhu, Bhairava, with a smiling face, spoke words to Hari.

3.9.s:
bhairava uvāca |
tvadvākpīyūṣapānena tṛpto'smi bahumānada |
svabhāvo'yaṃ hi sādhūnāṃ yattvaṃ vadasi māpate ||
3.9.d:
भैरव उवाच ।
त्वद्वाक्पीयूषपानेन तृप्तोऽस्मि बहुमानद ।
स्वभावोऽयं हि साधूनां यत्त्वं वदसि मापते ॥
3.9.m: Bhairava said: / By drinking the nectar of your speech, O giver of great respect, I am satisfied. / For this is the nature of the virtuous, which you speak, O lord of Lakṣmī.

3.9.s:
varaṃ vṛṇīṣva govinda varado'smi tavānagha |
agraṇīrmama bhaktānāṃ tvaṃ hare nirvikāravān ||
3.9.d:
वरं वृणीष्व गोविन्द वरदोऽस्मि तवानघ ।
अग्रणीर्मम भक्तानां त्वं हरे निर्विकारवान् ॥
3.9.m: Choose a boon, O Govinda; I am the giver of boons to you, O sinless one. / You are the foremost of my devotees, O Hari, free from change.

3.9.s:
no mādyanti tathā bhaikṣyairbhikṣavo'pyatisaṃskṛtaiḥ |
yathā mānasudhāpānairnanu bhikṣāṭanajvarāḥ ||
3.9.d:
नो माद्यन्ति तथा भैक्ष्यैर्भिक्षवोऽप्यतिसंस्कृतैः ।
यथा मानसुधापानैर्ननु भिक्षाटनज्वराः ॥
3.9.m: Mendicants are not so delighted even by highly refined alms / as those afflicted with the fever of wandering for alms [are delighted] by drinking the nectar of respect.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityākarṇya vacaḥ śambhorbhairavasya parātmanaḥ |
suprasannataro bhūtvā samavocanmaheśvaram ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचः शम्भोर्भैरवस्य परात्मनः ।
सुप्रसन्नतरो भूत्वा समवोचन्महेश्वरम् ॥
3.9.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having heard this speech of Śambhu, of Bhairava the supreme Self, / becoming exceedingly pleased, [Viṣṇu] spoke to Maheśvara.

3.9.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
eṣa eva varaḥ ślāghyo yadahaṃ devatādhipam |
paśyāmi tvāndevadeva manovāṇīpathātigam ||
3.9.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
एष एव वरः श्लाघ्यो यदहं देवताधिपम् ।
पश्यामि त्वान्देवदेव मनोवाणीपथातिगम् ॥
3.9.m: Viṣṇu said: / This indeed is a praiseworthy boon: that I behold the ruler of deities, / you, the God of gods, who transcend the range of mind and speech.

3.9.s:
adabhreyaṃ sudhādṛṣṭiranayā me mahotsavaḥ |
ayattnanidhilābho'yaṃ vīkṣaṇaṃ hara te satām ||
3.9.d:
अदभ्रेयं सुधादृष्टिरनया मे महोत्सवः ।
अयत्त्ननिधिलाभोऽयं वीक्षणं हर ते सताम् ॥
3.9.m: This gaze of yours, like nectar, is abundant; by this, I have a great festival. / This seeing of you, O Hara, is for the virtuous the effortless acquisition of a treasure.

3.9.s:
aviyogo'stu me deva tvadaṅghriyugalena vai |
eṣa eva varaḥ śambho nānyaṃ kaścid vṛṇe varam ||
3.9.d:
अवियोगोऽस्तु मे देव त्वदङ्घ्रियुगलेन वै ।
एष एव वरः शम्भो नान्यं कश्चिद् वृणे वरम् ॥
3.9.m: May there indeed be no separation for me, O God, from your pair of feet. / This alone is the boon, O Śambhu; I choose no other boon whatsoever.

3.9.s:
śrībhairava uvāca |
evaṃ bhavatu te tāta yattvayoktaṃ mahāmate |
sarveṣāmapi devānāṃ varadastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi ||
3.9.d:
श्रीभैरव उवाच ।
एवं भवतु ते तात यत्त्वयोक्तं महामते ।
सर्वेषामपि देवानां वरदस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥
3.9.m: The venerable Bhairava said: / Let it be so for you, my dear, as has been spoken by you, O wise one. / You shall also be the giver of boons to all the gods.

3.9.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
anugṛhyeti daityāriṃ kendrādribhuvane caran |
bheje'vimuktanagarīṃ nāmnā vārāṇasīṃ purīm ||
3.9.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
अनुगृह्येति दैत्यारिं केन्द्राद्रिभुवने चरन् ।
भेजेऽविमुक्तनगरीं नाम्ना वाराणसीं पुरीम् ॥
3.9.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having thus shown grace to the enemy of the Daityas, wandering through the worlds of the mountain of Indra and the like, / he reached the city Avimukta, the city named Vārāṇasī.

3.9.s:
kṣetre praviṣṭamātre'tha bhairave bhīṣaṇākṛtau |
hāhetyuktvā brahmahatyā pātālaṃ cāviśattadā ||
3.9.d:
क्षेत्रे प्रविष्टमात्रेऽथ भैरवे भीषणाकृतौ ।
हाहेत्युक्त्वा ब्रह्महत्या पातालं चाविशत्तदा ॥
3.9.m: The moment Bhairava of terrifying form entered the sacred field, / the brahminicide, crying 'Alas, alas!', then entered the underworld.

3.9.s:
kapālaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sadyo bhairavasya karāmbujāt |
papāta bhuvi tattīrthamabhūtkāpālamocanam ||
3.9.d:
कपालं ब्राह्मणः सद्यो भैरवस्य कराम्बुजात् ।
पपात भुवि तत्तीर्थमभूत्कापालमोचनम् ॥
3.9.m: Brahmā's skull immediately fell to the ground / from the lotus hand of Bhairava; that holy site became Kāpālamocana.

3.9.s:
kapālaṃ brahmaṇo rudraḥ sarveṣāmeva paśyatām |
hastātpatantamālokya nanarta parayā mudā ||
3.9.d:
कपालं ब्रह्मणो रुद्रः सर्वेषामेव पश्यताम् ।
हस्तात्पतन्तमालोक्य ननर्त परया मुदा ॥
3.9.m: Seeing Brahmā's skull falling from his hand / before the eyes of everyone, Rudra danced with supreme joy.

3.9.s:
vidheḥ kapālaṃ nāmuñcatkaramatyantadussaham |
parasya bhramataḥ kvāpi tatkāśyāṃ kṣaṇato'patat ||
3.9.d:
विधेः कपालं नामुञ्चत्करमत्यन्तदुस्सहम् ।
परस्य भ्रमतः क्वापि तत्काश्यां क्षणतोऽपतत् ॥
3.9.m: The utterly unbearable skull of Brahmā did not leave his hand / anywhere while the Supreme was wandering; in Kāśī, it fell in an instant.

3.9.s:
śūlino brahmaṇo hatyā nāpaiti sma ca yā kvacit |
sā kāśyāṃ kṣaṇato naṣṭā tasmātsevyā hi kāśikā ||
3.9.d:
शूलिनो ब्रह्मणो हत्या नापैति स्म च या क्वचित् ।
सा काश्यां क्षणतो नष्टा तस्मात्सेव्या हि काशिका ॥
3.9.m: And the murder of Brahmā, which did not depart from the trident-bearer anywhere, / perished in an instant in Kāśī; therefore, Kāśī is certainly to be resorted to.

3.9.s:
kapālamocanaṃ kāśyāṃ yaḥ smarettīrthamuttamam |
ihānyatrāpi yatpāpaṃ kṣipraṃ tasya praṇaśyati ||
3.9.d:
कपालमोचनं काश्यां यः स्मरेत्तीर्थमुत्तमम् ।
इहान्यत्रापि यत्पापं क्षिप्रं तस्य प्रणश्यति ॥
3.9.m: Whoever remembers the excellent holy site Kāpālamocana in Kāśī, / whatever sin is his, here or elsewhere, quickly perishes.

3.9.s:
āgatya tīrthapravare snānaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ |
tarpayitvā pitṝndevānmucyate brahmahatyayā ||
3.9.d:
आगत्य तीर्थप्रवरे स्नानं कृत्वा विधानतः ।
तर्पयित्वा पितॄन्देवान्मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
3.9.m: Having come to the most excellent holy site, having bathed according to the rules, / and having offered libations to the ancestors and gods, one is freed from brahminicide.

3.9.s:
kapālamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ puraskṛtvā tu bhairavaḥ |
tatraiva tasthau bhaktānāṃ bhakṣayannaghasantatim ||
3.9.d:
कपालमोचनं तीर्थं पुरस्कृत्वा तु भैरवः ।
तत्रैव तस्थौ भक्तानां भक्षयन्नघसन्ततिम् ॥
3.9.m: Having honored the holy site Kāpālamocana, Bhairava / remained right there, consuming the succession of sins of his devotees.

3.9.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ tu mārgasya māsasya parameśvaraḥ |
āvirbabhūva sallīlo bhairavātmā satāṃ priyaḥ ||
3.9.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां तु मार्गस्य मासस्य परमेश्वरः ।
आविर्बभूव सल्लीलो भैरवात्मा सतां प्रियः ॥
3.9.m: On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, Parameśvara, / playful in nature, embodying Bhairava and dear to the virtuous, manifested.

3.9.s:
mārgaśīrṣāsitāṣṭamyāṃ kālabhairavasannidhau |
upoṣya jāgaraṃ kurvanmahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
3.9.d:
मार्गशीर्षासिताष्टम्यां कालभैरवसन्निधौ ।
उपोष्य जागरं कुर्वन्महापापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
3.9.m: Having fasted and kept vigil in the presence of Kālabhairava / on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, one is released from great sins.

3.9.s:
anyatrāpi naro bhaktyā tad vrataṃ yaḥ kariṣyati |
sajāgaraṃ mahāpāpairmukto yāsyati sadgatim ||
3.9.d:
अन्यत्रापि नरो भक्त्या तद् व्रतं यः करिष्यति ।
सजागरं महापापैर्मुक्तो यास्यति सद्गतिम् ॥
3.9.m: Even elsewhere, the person who undertakes that observance with devotion, / keeping vigil, will be freed from great sins and attain the good destination.

3.9.s:
anekajanmaniyutairyatkṛtaṃ jantubhistvagham |
tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti kālabhairavadarśanāt ||
3.9.d:
अनेकजन्मनियुतैर्यत्कृतं जन्तुभिस्त्वघम् ।
तत्सर्वं विलयं याति कालभैरवदर्शनात् ॥
3.9.m: Whatever sin has been committed by living beings through many millions of births, / all that dissolves away from the sight of Kālabhairava.

3.9.s:
kālabhairavabhaktānāṃ pātakāni karoti yaḥ |
sa mūḍho duḥkhito bhūtvā punardurgatimāpnuyāt ||
3.9.d:
कालभैरवभक्तानां पातकानि करोति यः ।
स मूढो दुःखितो भूत्वा पुनर्दुर्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
3.9.m: Whoever commits wrongful deeds against the devotees of Kālabhairava, / that fool, having become miserable, will again attain an evil destination.

3.9.s:
viśveśvare'pi ye bhaktā no bhaktāḥ kālabhairave |
te labhante mahāduḥkhaṃ kāśyāṃ caiva viśeṣataḥ ||
3.9.d:
विश्वेश्वरेऽपि ये भक्ता नो भक्ताः कालभैरवे ।
ते लभन्ते महादुःखं काश्यां चैव विशेषतः ॥
3.9.m: Those who, though devoted to Viśveśvara, are not devoted to Kālabhairava / obtain great misery, especially in Kāśī.

3.9.s:
vārāṇasyāmuṣitvā yo bhairavaṃ na bhajennaraḥ |
tasya pāpāni varddhante śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī ||
3.9.d:
वाराणस्यामुषित्वा यो भैरवं न भजेन्नरः ।
तस्य पापानि वर्द्धन्ते शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी ॥
3.9.m: The man who, having dwelt in Vārāṇasī, does not worship Bhairava, / his sins increase like the moon in the bright fortnight.

3.9.s:
kālarājaṃ na yaḥ kāśyāṃ pratibhūtāṣṭamīkujam |
bhajettasya kṣayaṃ puṇyaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe yathā śaśī ||
3.9.d:
कालराजं न यः काश्यां प्रतिभूताष्टमीकुजम् ।
भजेत्तस्य क्षयं पुण्यं कृष्णपक्षे यथा शशी ॥
3.9.m: Whoever does not worship Kālarāja in Kāśī on every fourteenth, eighth, and Tuesday, / his merit diminishes like the moon in the dark fortnight.

3.9.s:
śrutvākhyānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmahatyāpanodakam |
bhairavotpattisaṃjñaṃ ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
3.9.d:
श्रुत्वाख्यानमिदं पुण्यं ब्रह्महत्यापनोदकम् ।
भैरवोत्पत्तिसंज्ञं च सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
3.9.m: Having heard this sacred narrative that dispels brahminicide, / named 'The Origin of Bhairava', one is released from all sins.

3.9.s:
bandhanāgārasaṃstho'pi prāpto'pi vipadaṃ parām |
prādurbhāvaṃ bhairavasya śrutvā mucyeta saṅkaṭāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.9.d:
बन्धनागारसंस्थोऽपि प्राप्तोऽपि विपदं पराम् ।
प्रादुर्भावं भैरवस्य श्रुत्वा मुच्येत सङ्कटात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.9.m:
Even one stationed in prison, even one who has attained supreme misfortune, / having heard of the manifestation of Bhairava, would be freed from distress.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, named 'The Description of the Sport of Bhairava's Incarnation', in the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, the third [book] in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

3.10.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
vidhvaṃsī dakṣayajñasya vīrabhadrāhvayaḥ prabhoḥ |
avatāraśca vijñeyaḥ śivasya paramātmanaḥ ||
3.10.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
विध्वंसी दक्षयज्ञस्य वीरभद्राह्वयः प्रभोः ।
अवतारश्च विज्ञेयः शिवस्य परमात्मनः ॥
3.10.m: Nandīśvara said: / The destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, named Vīrabhadra, / is to be known as an incarnation of the Lord, Śiva, the supreme Self.

3.10.s:
satīcaritre kathitaṃ caritaṃ tasya kṛtsnaśaḥ |
śrutaṃ tvayāpi bahudhā nātaḥ proktaṃ suvistarāt ||
3.10.d:
सतीचरित्रे कथितं चरितं तस्य कृत्स्नशः ।
श्रुतं त्वयापि बहुधा नातः प्रोक्तं सुविस्तरात् ॥
3.10.m: His story was told completely in the story of Satī; / it was also heard by you in many ways, hence it is not told here in great detail.

3.10.s:
ataḥ paraṃ muniśreṣṭha bhavatsnehād bravīmi tat |
śārdūlākhyāvatāraṃ ca śaṅkarasya prabhoḥ śṛṇu ||
3.10.d:
अतः परं मुनिश्रेष्ठ भवत्स्नेहाद् ब्रवीमि तत् ।
शार्दूलाख्यावतारं च शङ्करस्य प्रभोः शृणु ॥
3.10.m: Beyond this, O best of sages, out of affection for you I tell it; / hear also of the incarnation named Śarabha of the lord Śaṅkara.

3.10.s:
sadāśivena devānāṃ hitārthaṃ rūpamadbhutam |
śārabhaṃ ca dhṛtaṃ divyaṃ jvalajjvālāsamaprabham ||
3.10.d:
सदाशिवेन देवानां हितार्थं रूपमद्भुतम् ।
शारभं च धृतं दिव्यं ज्वलज्ज्वालासमप्रभम् ॥
3.10.m: For the welfare of the gods, Sadāśiva assumed a wondrous, / divine form of Śarabha, equal in luster to blazing flames.

3.10.s:
śivāvatārā amitāḥ sadbhaktahitakārakāḥ |
saṅkhyā na śakyate kartuṃ teṣāṃ ca munisattamāḥ ||
3.10.d:
शिवावतारा अमिताः सद्भक्तहितकारकाः ।
सङ्ख्या न शक्यते कर्तुं तेषां च मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
3.10.m: The incarnations of Śiva are limitless, bringing benefit to true devotees; / it is not possible, O best of sages, to make an enumeration of them.

3.10.s:
ākāśasya ca tārāṇāṃ reṇukānāṃ kṣitestathā |
āsārāṇāṃ ca vṛddhena bahukalpaiḥ kadāpi hi ||
3.10.d:
आकाशस्य च ताराणां रेणुकानां क्षितेस्तथा ।
आसाराणां च वृद्धेन बहुकल्पैः कदापि हि ॥
3.10.m: Even over many kalpas, of the stars in the sky and of the particles of dust on the earth, / and of torrents of rain, an enumeration might at some time be made by a wise elder

3.10.s:
saṅkhyā viśakyate kartuṃ suprājñairbahujanmabhiḥ |
na vai śivāvatārāṇāṃ satyaṃ jānīhi madvacaḥ ||
3.10.d:
सङ्ख्या विशक्यते कर्तुं सुप्राज्ञैर्बहुजन्मभिः ।
न वै शिवावताराणां सत्यं जानीहि मद्वचः ॥
3.10.m: through many births by the very wise, / but never of Śiva's incarnations; know my word to be true.

3.10.s:
tathāpi ca yathābuddhyā kathayāmi yathāśrutam |
caritraṃ śārabhaṃ divyaṃ paramaiśvaryasūcakam ||
3.10.d:
तथापि च यथाबुद्ध्या कथयामि यथाश्रुतम् ।
चरित्रं शारभं दिव्यं परमैश्वर्यसूचकम् ॥
3.10.m: Nevertheless, according to my intellect and as heard [by me], I will tell / the divine story of Śarabha, indicative of supreme sovereign power.

3.10.s:
jayaśca vijayaścaiva bhavadbhiḥ śāpitau yadā |
tadā ditisutau dvau tāvabhūtāṃ kaśyapānmune ||
3.10.d:
जयश्च विजयश्चैव भवद्भिः शापितौ यदा ।
तदा दितिसुतौ द्वौ तावभूतां कश्यपान्मुने ॥
3.10.m: When Jaya and Vijaya were cursed by you [sages], / then those two sons of Diti were born from Kaśyapa, O sage.

3.10.s:
hiraṇyakaśipuścādyo hiraṇyākṣo'nujo balī |
devarṣipārṣadau jātau tau dvāvapi diteḥ sutau ||
3.10.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुश्चाद्यो हिरण्याक्षोऽनुजो बली ।
देवर्षिपार्षदौ जातौ तौ द्वावपि दितेः सुतौ ॥
3.10.m: Hiraṇyakaśipu was the elder, and the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa was the younger brother; / both attendants of the divine sage were born as sons of Diti.

3.10.s:
pṛthvyuddhāre vidhātrā va prārthito hi purā prabhuḥ |
hiraṇyākṣaṃ jaghānāsau viṣṇurvārāharūpadhṛk ||
3.10.d:
पृथ्व्युद्धारे विधात्रा व प्रार्थितो हि पुरा प्रभुः ।
हिरण्याक्षं जघानासौ विष्णुर्वाराहरूपधृक् ॥
3.10.m: Formerly, when the earth was lifted up, the Lord was petitioned by the creator; / that Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a boar, slew Hiraṇyākṣa.

3.10.s:
taṃ śrutvā bhrātaraṃ vīraṃ nihataṃ prāṇasannibham |
cukopa haraye'tīva hiraṇyakaśipurmune ||
3.10.d:
तं श्रुत्वा भ्रातरं वीरं निहतं प्राणसन्निभम् ।
चुकोप हरयेऽतीव हिरण्यकशिपुर्मुने ॥
